**Expanded App Store (24 apps)**
![App Store](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a917ab59-d8c1-45af-8d25-9a1c6f0d7808)

**Browser with Search**
![Browser](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bfa0f122-14aa-4ba9-a54c-95c81f515092)

**Desktop with Terminal**
![Desktop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3c9e601-f5fd-4aca-8a60-01ad96e90604)

## Notes

Proxy endpoints configured with proper header forwarding for restriction bypass. Actual content loading subject to external site CORS/CSP policies and deployment environment network configuration.

author: vityaded
body:
### Motivation
- Prevent detour/revisit/check flows from picking or generating out-of-range (virtual) exercise indices that cause topic drift.
- Keep LLM generation allowed but anchored to unit rules and bounded so it cannot invent “exercise 11” for a unit with only 1..N real exercises. 
- Provide deterministic, reproducible selection of exercises per `due.id` and better logging for future diagnosis.

### Description
- Implemented real-exercise inventory helpers in `src/bot/exercise_inventory.py` and use them to compute `unit_real_exercise_indices` and dataset-driven `max_real` per unit. 
- Reworked due selection in `src/bot/handlers.py` to pick deterministic shuffled real indices (seeded by `due.id:unit_key:kind`), map `due.exercise_index` to a position within the selected list, and always call `ensure_unit_exercise` with the mapped real index. 
- Added constrained LLM generation in `src/bot/exercise_generator.py` and `src/bot/llm.py` by passing full unit rule context, a `topic_lock` instruction, bounding generation to index 1..2 when no real exercises exist, and performing a single deterministic forbidden-marker validation/regenerate pass. 
- Added maintenance helpers `src/bot/db_maintenance.py` plus admin command `purge_generated_exercises` and startup logging via `log_out_of_range_exercises` to report (but not auto-delete) out-of-range generated rows. 

### Testing
- Added `tests/test_detour_real_exercises.py` and adjusted existing tests to exercise detour/revisit selection and LLM fallback behavior. 
- Ran the full test suite with `pytest -q`. 
- Result: all tests passed (`26 passed`).

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a vertical Y-axis for shared stats charts with generated tick labels so viewers can read scale values without cluttering bars.  
- Make bar spacing and widths adaptive to the number of data points so charts fit inside their panels across admin and seller pages.  
- Keep value disclosure on hover/focus and keyboard accessibility for each bar.  
- Preserve existing `valueFormatter` usage so callers don't need to change formatting logic.  

### Description
- Reworked the chart to render vertical columns and renamed the sizing helper to `toHeight` that computes bar height relative to `maxValue`.  
- Added computed properties `dataLength`, `yTicks`, `barGap`, `minBarWidth`, and `barLayoutStyle` to generate Y-axis ticks and responsive grid layout (using `gridTemplateColumns` and `gap`).  
- Updated template to include a left Y-axis (`.bar-chart__y-axis`) and a bars grid (`.bar-chart__bars`), kept `data-value` tooltip and `tabindex="0"` for accessibility.  
- Adjusted scoped styles for the grid layout, bar appearance, hover/focus tooltip, and removed the fixed `max-width` constraint so bars size responsively.  

### Testing
- Launched the dev server with `npm run dev` and ran a Playwright script to navigate to `/admin/live/sanctions` and capture a screenshot, which succeeded.  
- Ran `npm run build`, which failed due to pre-existing TypeScript errors in unrelated files and not from the chart changes.

author: copilot
body:
Implements platform abstraction to separate window/context management from graphics API, improving RHI architecture by removing direct platform dependencies.

## Architecture Changes

- **New Platform Layer**: `Platform.h`, `PlatformTypes.h`, `Platform.cpp` providing:
  - Cross-platform window creation and management (`IPlatform`, `IPlatformWindow`)
  - Graphics context lifecycle (make current, swap buffers, proc address loading)
  - Display/monitor queries with safe string handling
  - Compile-time platform detection (Windows/Linux/macOS)

- **RHI Decoupling**: 
  - Removed GLFW includes and initialization from `OpenGLRHI.cpp`
  - RHI now validates existing OpenGL context instead of creating one
  - Context creation delegated to Platform layer

- **Renderer Refactoring**:
  - Replaced `GLFWwindow*` with `std::shared_ptr<IPlatformWindow>`
  - GLAD initialization uses platform's `getProcAddress()` via thread-local wrapper
  - Removed all direct GLFW dependencies

## Code Example

Before:
```cpp
// Renderer directly managing GLFW
glfwInit();
window = glfwCreateWindow(width, height, title, nullptr, nullptr);
glfwMakeContextCurrent(window);
gladLoadGLLoader((GLADloadproc)glfwGetProcAddress);
```

After:
```cpp
// Platform abstraction
platform = Platform::createPlatform();
platform->initialize();
window = platform->createWindow(desc);
window->makeContextCurrent();
// GLAD uses platform's getProcAddress internally
```

## Implementation Details

- GLFW backend supports all platforms (Windows/Linux/macOS)
- Thread-local storage ensures safe GLAD initialization
- `DisplayInfo` uses `std::string` to prevent dangling pointers
- Null checks added for disconnected monitors
- Build system updated to include `src/Platform/*.cpp`

## Documentation

- `PLATFORM.md`: Platform API reference and usage patterns
- `PLATFORM_IMPLEMENTATION.md`: Migration guide and design rationale
- Updated `ARCHITECTURE.md` with Platform layer in system diagram
- `CHANGELOG.md` bumped to v0.2.0

Foundation for future native implementations (Win32, X11, Cocoa) without touching application code.

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> ## Özet
> Turn skill'leri (3, 4, 5, 28) için yön seçimi UI'ı ekle. Kullanıcı skill'e başlamadan önce LEFT veya RIGHT seçecek.
> 
> ## Mevcut Sorun
> Turn skill'lerinde "turn left or right" ifadesi backend'de 2 ayrı step oluşturuyor veya belirsiz kalıyor. Kullanıcı hangi yöne döneceğini bilmiyor.
> 
> ## Yapılacaklar
> 
> ### 1. DirectionSelectionPanel UI
> 
> Yeni bir panel oluştur:
> ```
> DirectionSelectionPanel/
> ├── Background (semi-transparent)
> ├── Title Text: "Select Turn Direction"
> ├── LeftButton 
> │   ├── Text: "← LEFT (A)"
> │   └── OnClick: OnDirectionSelected("left")
> └── RightButton
>     ├── Text: "RIGHT (D) →"
>     └── OnClick: OnDirectionSelected("right")
> ```
> 
> ### 2. ExerciseManager.cs Güncellemesi
> 
> Turn skill'lerini tanımla:
> ```csharp
> private HashSet<string> turnSkills = new HashSet<string> 
> { 
>     "3",   // Turns while moving forwards (90°)
>     "4",   // Turns while moving backwards (90°)
>     "5",   // Turns in place (180°)
>     "28"   // Turns in wheelie position (180��)
> };
> ```
> 
> `OnSkillSelected()` metodunu güncelle:
> - Eğer skill turn skill ise → DirectionSelectionPanel göster
> - Değilse → direkt StartSkillTraining çağır
> 
> Yeni metodlar ekle:
> ```csharp
> private string pendingSkillId;
> 
> public void OnDirectionSelected(string direction)
> {
>     directionSelectionPanel.SetActive(false);
>     string question = GetDirectionalQuestion(pendingSkillId, direction);
>     StartSkillWithQuestion(pendingSkillId, question);
> }
> 
> private string GetDirectionalQuestion(string skillId, string direction)
> {
>     return skillId switch
>     {
>         "3" => $"How do I turn {direction} 90 degrees while moving forward in a wheelchair?",
>         "4" => $"How do I turn {direction} 90 degrees while moving backward in a wheelchair?",
>         "5" => $"How do I turn {direction} 180 degrees in place while sitting in a wheelchair?",
>         "28" => $"How do I turn {direction} 180 degrees in place while in a wheelie position?",
>         _ => GetDefaultQuestion(skillId)
>     };
> }
> ```
> 
> ### 3. Inspector References
> 
> ExerciseManager'a yeni referanslar ekle:
> ```csharp
> [Header("Direction Selection")]
> public GameObject directionSelectionPanel;
> public Button turnLeftButton;
> public Button turnRightButton;
> ```
> 
> ### 4. Button Event Binding
> 
> Start() metodunda button listener'ları ekle:
> ```csharp
> if (turnLeftButton != null)
>     turnLeftButton.onClick.AddListener(() => OnDirectionSelected("left"));
> if (turnRightButton != null)
>     turnRightButton.onClick.AddListener(() => OnDirectionSelected("right"));
> ```
> 
> ## Kullanıcı Akışı
> 
> ```
> 1. Kullanıcı "Skill 3: Turn while moving forward" seçer
> 2. DirectionSelectionPanel açılır
> 3. Kullanıcı "LEFT" veya "RIGHT" butonuna basar
> 4. Backend'e spesifik soru gider: "How do I turn LEFT 90 degrees..."
> 5. GPT doğru action'ı döndürür: turn_left
> 6. Tutorial başlar
> ```
> 
> ## Dosyalar
> - `Assets/Scripts/ExerciseManager.cs` - Ana değişiklikler
> - Yeni prefab/UI elementi gerekebilir
>

> Bu değişiklik `wheelchair-skills-rag` reposundaki GPT action generation PR'ı ile birlikte çalışacak.

Route ordering in CrudApiPlugin causes JSONPath parsing errors when generic patterns precede specific ones. A request to `/below/15` matches `/{product-id}` first if defined earlier, resulting in `$.[?(@.id == below)]` and a parsing failure.

## Changes

- Added **CrudApiPlugin** section to best practices documenting route matching behavior
- Included correct and incorrect ordering examples with JSONPath queries

## Example

```json
// ✓ Correct: specific before generic
{
  "action": "getMany",
  "url": "/below/{max-price}",
  "query": "$.[?(@.price < {max-price})]"
},
{
  "action": "getOne",
  "url": "/{product-id}",
  "query": "$.[?(@.id == {product-id})]"
}
```

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 
> ----
> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>Route ordering in CrudApiPlugin affects JSONPath query parsing</issue_title>
> <issue_description>## Agent reasoning
> 
> The existing queries work fine. The issue with the `getMany` action was that I was using an incorrect URL pattern that conflicted with the `getOne` action. When I used `/cheap/{max-price}`, it was probably being matched by the `getOne` action's `/{product-id}` pattern first.
> 
> Looking at the error message again: "Unexpected character while parsing path query: c" - the "c" suggests it's trying to parse "cheap" as if it were a product-id in the `getOne` query.
> 
> The solution is to use a URL pattern that doesn't conflict with the existing /`{product-id}` pattern. I should use something more distinct, or put the more specific route first in the actions array. In Dev Proxy, more specific routes should come first.
> 
> Let me add a `getMany` action with a more unique URL pattern that won't conflict, and place it before the `getOne` action to ensure it's matched first.
> 
> The agent ran `Get best practices` tool before attempting to update the file.
> 
> ## Problem
> 
> When adding a new `getMany` action to an existing CrudApiPlugin configuration, requests failed with a Newtonsoft.Json parsing error:
> 
> ```
> Unexpected character while parsing path query: c
> ```
> 
> ## Root Cause
> 
> **Route ordering matters.** The new action was placed *after* an existing `getOne` action with a catch-all URL pattern:
> 
> ```json
> {
> 	"action": "getOne",
> 	"url": "/{product-id}",
> 	"query": "$.[?(@.id == {product-id})]"
> },
> {
> 	"action": "getMany",
> 	"url": "/below/{max-price}",
> 	"query": "$.[?(@.price < {max-price})]"
> }
> ```
> 
> When requesting `/below/15`, the `/{product-id}` pattern matched first, treating "below" as the product-id. This resulted in the query `$.[?(@.id == below)]` being executed, which failed because "below" is not a valid value for the JSONPath expression.
> 
> ## Solution
> 
> Place more specific routes **before** catch-all patterns:
> 
> ```json
> {
> 	"action": "getMany",
> 	"url": "/below/{max-price}",
> 	"query": "$.[?(@.price < {max-price})]"
> },
> {
> 	"action": "getOne",
> 	"url": "/{product-id}",
> 	"query": "$.[?(@.id == {product-id})]"
> }
> ```
> 
> ## Key Takeaway
> 
> Actions in the CrudApiPlugin are matched in the order they're defined. Always define actions with more specific URL patterns (e.g., `/below/{value}`, `/category/{name}`) before generic catch-all patterns (e.g., `/{id}`).</issue_description>
>

author: srhb
body:
Two main changes,

- allow nix-instantiate to realise paths (useful for eg. realising
  inputs from flake-compat if the index is really from a thinly-wrapped
  flake)
- Allow the index to not be a function, again useful for more flakeful
  setups that don't take the usual (old-nix style) `{ pkgs ? ... }:`.
  This is necessary because unlike nix-build, nix-instantiate --eval
  --expr will not prefill the empty argset.

# Ratatui TUI Migration

## Summary

This PR completes the migration from **skim** to **nucleo + ratatui** for the terminal user interface. The new TUI provides better control, faster fuzzy matching, and modern UI features while maintaining full backward compatibility with existing workflows.

## What Changed

### Dependencies
- **Removed**: `skim` (was optional)
- **Added**: 
  - `nucleo 0.5` - Fast fuzzy matching engine (10-100x faster for large lists)
  - `ratatui 0.30` - Modern terminal UI framework
  - `crossterm 0.28` - Cross-platform terminal handling

### Feature Flags
- **Removed**: `skim-tui` and `ratatui-tui` feature flags
- TUI dependencies are now always included (non-optional)
- Only remaining feature: `syntax-highlighting` (default, uses syntect)

### Code Changes
- Deleted `src/ui/skim_adapter.rs` (~400 lines)
- Removed all `#[cfg(feature = "...")]` conditional compilation
- Renamed `ratatui_bindings()` → `bindings()` in keybind config
- Applied `cargo fmt --all`

## New TUI Features

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Modal text input** | Fuzzy autocomplete for tag entry with Tab completion |
| **Confirmation dialogs** | Safe prompts for destructive actions (delete from DB) |
| **F1 Help overlay** | Shows all available keybinds in current context |
| **F2 Refine search** | Edit search criteria without leaving the TUI |
| **Native syntax highlighting** | Direct syntect → ratatui rendering (no ANSI parsing) |
| **Preview scrolling** | Shift+↑/↓ for navigating preview pane |

## Keybinds (Unchanged)

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `Ctrl+T` | Add tags to selected files |
| `Ctrl+R` | Remove tags from selected files |
| `Ctrl+D` | Delete files from database |
| `Ctrl+O` | Open in default application |
| `Ctrl+Y` | Copy file paths to clipboard |
| `Tab` | Toggle multi-select |
| `Enter` | Confirm selection |
| `Esc` | Cancel / go back |
| `F1` | Show help |
| `F2` | Refine search criteria |

## Breaking Changes

**None** - All CLI commands and workflows work exactly as before.

## Testing

```bash
# Run tests
cargo test

# Build and run
cargo build --release
./target/release/tagr browse

# Test key features
tagr browse                    # Basic browse
tagr browse -t rust            # Browse with tag filter
tagr browse -v modified:today  # Browse with virtual tags
```

## Performance

- Fuzzy matching is 10-100x faster with nucleo (especially for large file sets)
- Preview rendering is more efficient with native ratatui styles
- No ANSI parsing overhead

## Screenshots

The TUI looks similar to before but with improved responsiveness and new overlay features (F1 help, F2 refine search, modal dialogs).

## Version

Bumped to **v0.8.0**

## Checklist

- [x] All tests pass (`cargo test`)
- [x] Build succeeds (`cargo build --release`)
- [x] Clippy passes with pedantic/nursery lints
- [x] Documentation updated (README, CHANGELOG, config examples)
- [x] No breaking changes to CLI or library API

author: ahamed-ali
body:
### Root Cause of the issue



- `Stepper_SetIncrementAndVerifyValueChange` and `Stepper_SetIncrementValue_VerifyIncrement` in the candidate failed because the previous test, Stepper_ResetToInitialState_VerifyDefaultValues, updated the Minimum value to 10.

- When the next test (Stepper_SetIncrementAndVerifyValueChange) runs, a new ViewModel is created and the default values (Value = 0, Minimum = 0) are set in StepperFeature. However, MapValue is called first during the time, the Minimum value still retains the value 10 from the previous test. Although MAUI correctly updates PlatformStepper.Value, the native UIStepper automatically clamps the value based on the old Minimum value, causing the test to fail.

### Description of Change



- Before updating `platformStepper.Value`, the code first checks if MinimumValue needs updating and applies it. This ensures iOS always clamps against the current/correct MinimumValue, not a stale one.

#### Example Scenario

Old state: Min=5, Value=5
New state: Min=0, Value=2
Without fix: If Value is set first (to 2), iOS sees Min=5 (stale) and clamps Value back to 5
With fix: Min is updated to 0 first, then Value is set to 2 successfully


### Regressed PR 

#32939

author: copilot
body:
Turn skills generate ambiguous "turn left or right" instructions in the backend, causing unclear tutorial steps. Users now select LEFT or RIGHT before training begins, sending direction-specific questions to the RAG system.

## Changes

**ExerciseManager.cs**
- Added `turnSkills` HashSet (skills 3, 4, 5, 28) to trigger direction selection flow
- Added UI references: `directionSelectionPanel`, `turnLeftButton`, `turnRightButton`
- Modified `OnSkillSelected()` to show direction panel for turn skills, bypass for others
- Added `OnDirectionSelected(direction)` to handle user choice and start training
- Added `GetDirectionalQuestion()` to generate direction-specific questions:
  ```csharp
  "3" + "left" → "How do I turn left 90 degrees while moving forward in a wheelchair?"
  "28" + "right" → "How do I turn right 180 degrees in place while in a wheelie position?"
  ```
- Refactored `StartSkillTraining()` → `StartSkillWithQuestion()` to support custom questions
- Fixed Skill 5 question to match turn skill definition (was "roll 100m", now "turn 180°")
- Cached delegate references for proper button cleanup

**Documentation**
- Added DirectionSelectionPanel setup instructions in README.md
- Created IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md with Unity Editor configuration steps

## Flow

```
Turn skill selected → Direction panel shows → User clicks LEFT/RIGHT 
→ Backend receives "...turn {direction}..." → GPT generates turn_{direction} action
```

Non-turn skills bypass the panel entirely.

## Manual Unity Editor Setup Required

UI panel must be created manually (structure documented in IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md):
- Create DirectionSelectionPanel with semi-transparent background
- Add TitleText, LeftButton ("← LEFT (A)"), RightButton ("RIGHT (D) →")
- Wire references in ExerciseManager Inspector
- Set panel inactive by default

Button events bind automatically in code—no manual OnClick configuration needed.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> ## Özet
> Turn skill'leri (3, 4, 5, 28) için yön seçimi UI'ı ekle. Kullanıcı skill'e başlamadan önce LEFT veya RIGHT seçecek.
> 
> ## Mevcut Sorun
> Turn skill'lerinde "turn left or right" ifadesi backend'de 2 ayrı step oluşturuyor veya belirsiz kalıyor. Kullanıcı hangi yöne döneceğini bilmiyor.
> 
> ## Yapılacaklar
> 
> ### 1. DirectionSelectionPanel UI
> 
> Yeni bir panel oluştur:
> ```
> DirectionSelectionPanel/
> ├── Background (semi-transparent)
> ├── Title Text: "Select Turn Direction"
> ├── LeftButton 
> │   ├── Text: "← LEFT (A)"
> │   └── OnClick: OnDirectionSelected("left")
> └── RightButton
>     ├── Text: "RIGHT (D) →"
>     └── OnClick: OnDirectionSelected("right")
> ```
> 
> ### 2. ExerciseManager.cs Güncellemesi
> 
> Turn skill'lerini tanımla:
> ```csharp
> private HashSet<string> turnSkills = new HashSet<string> 
> { 
>     "3",   // Turns while moving forwards (90°)
>     "4",   // Turns while moving backwards (90°)
>     "5",   // Turns in place (180°)
>     "28"   // Turns in wheelie position (180°)
> };
> ```
> 
> `OnSkillSelected()` metodunu güncelle:
> - Eğer skill turn skill ise → DirectionSelectionPanel göster
> - Değilse → direkt StartSkillTraining çağır
> 
> Yeni metodlar ekle:
> ```csharp
> private string pendingSkillId;
> 
> public void OnDirectionSelected(string direction)
> {
>     directionSelectionPanel.SetActive(false);
>     string question = GetDirectionalQuestion(pendingSkillId, direction);
>     StartSkillWithQuestion(pendingSkillId, question);
> }
> 
> private string GetDirectionalQuestion(string skillId, string direction)
> {
>     return skillId switch
>     {
>         "3" => $"How do I turn {direction} 90 degrees while moving forward in a wheelchair?",
>         "4" => $"How do I turn {direction} 90 degrees while moving backward in a wheelchair?",
>         "5" => $"How do I turn {direction} 180 degrees in place while sitting in a wheelchair?",
>         "28" => $"How do I turn {direction} 180 degrees in place while in a wheelie position?",
>         _ => GetDefaultQuestion(skillId)
>     };
> }
> ```
> 
> ### 3. Inspector References
> 
> ExerciseManager'a yeni referanslar ekle:
> ```csharp
> [Header("Direction Selection")]
> public GameObject directionSelectionPanel;
> public Button turnLeftButton;
> public Button turnRightButton;
> ```
> 
> ### 4. Button Event Binding
> 
> Start() metodunda button listener'ları ekle:
> ```csharp
> if (turnLeftButton != null)
>     turnLeftButton.onClick.AddListener(() => OnDirectionSelected("left"));
> if (turnRightButton != null)
>     turnRightButton.onClick.AddListener(() => OnDirectionSelected("right"));
> ```
> 
> ## Kullanıcı Akışı
> 
> ```
> 1. Kullanıcı "Skill 3: Turn while moving forward" seçer
> 2. DirectionSelectionPanel açılır
> 3. Kullanıcı "LEFT" veya "RIGHT" butonuna basar
> 4. Backend'e spesifik soru gider: "How do I turn LEFT 90 degrees..."
> 5. GPT doğru action'ı döndürür: turn_left
> 6. Tutorial başlar
> ```
> 
> ## Dosyalar
> - `Assets/Scripts/ExerciseManager.cs` - Ana değişiklikler
> - Yeni prefab/UI elementi gerekebilir
> 
> ## Not
> Bu değişiklik `wheelchair-skills-rag` reposundaki GPT action generation PR'ı ile birlikte çalışacak.

body:
## Fix txt2po handling of line feeds around text block

### Plan:
- [x] Verify and reproduce the issue with test case
- [x] Analyze the root cause in po2txt.py merge_stores() method
- [x] Implement fix: Sort units by source length (descending) before replacement
- [x] Add test case to test_po2txt.py to prevent regression
- [x] Run tests to verify fix works
- [x] Run code review and security checks
- [x] Address pre-commit errors (ruff format, typos)
- [x] Improve code readability per reviewer feedback
- [x] Use inline typos ignore as requested

### Changes Made:
1. **Fixed po2txt.py merge_stores() method**: Sort translation units by source string length in descending order before performing replacements
2. **Added test case**: Added `test_substring_replacement` to prevent regression
3. **Improved code readability**: Applied ruff formatting to break down complex conditional into multiple lines (addresses reviewer feedback)
4. **Used inline typos ignore**: Added codespell:ignore comments for German word "vor" instead of creating separate config file

### Issue Summary:
The `merge_stores()` method in po2txt.py uses simple string replacement which causes issues when shorter strings are substrings of longer strings. For example:
- "Constructor" → "Konstrukteur" 
- "Constructors" → "Konstrukteure"

When "Constructor" is replaced first, it also replaces the "Constructor" part in "Constructors", resulting in "Konstrukteurs" instead of "Konstrukteure".

### Solution:
Sort translation units by source string length in descending order before performing replacements, ensuring longer strings are replaced first and won't be affected by shorter substring replacements.

### Testing:
- All 19 tests pass
- Manual verification with po2txt command confirms correct behavior
- Edge cases tested: multiple overlapping substrings, identical length strings, very short strings
- Code review passed
- Security check passed (0 alerts)
- Pre-commit checks pass with inline typos ignore

author: elijahmathews
body:
### Description
This PR updates the repository to reflect that Python 3.9 reached its official End-of-Life (EOL) status in October 2025 ([PEP 596](https://peps.python.org/pep-0596/)) and NumPy 1.*x* reached its EOL status in September 2025 ([link](https://endoflife.date/numpy)). It drops support for Python 3.9 and NumPy 1.*x*, bumps the minimum supported versions to Python 3.10 and NumPy 2.0, and ensures the package is tested against the latest stable release of Python (Python 3.14).

Additionally, this PR overhauls Prospector's packaging configuration to meet modern Python standards (PEP [621](https://peps.python.org/pep-0621/)/[639](https://peps.python.org/pep-0639/)). It centralizes metadata, configuration, and dependencies into `pyproject.toml`, removing the need to maintain the redundant `requirements.txt` file.

### Changes
* **Packaging Overhaul:**
    * Migrated all project metadata and dependencies to `pyproject.toml` ([PEP 621](https://peps.python.org/pep-0621/) compliant).
    * Adopted the new `license` string standard ([PEP 639](https://peps.python.org/pep-0639/)) and upgraded build requirements to `setuptools>=77`.
    * Configured automatic package discovery (including fixing the discovery of `prospect.sources.agn_data`).
    * Reduced `requirements.txt` to a single `-e .` entry.
* **Dependencies:**
    * Bumped `requires-python` to `>=3.10`.
    * **NumPy 2.0 Compatibility:** Explicitly updated minimum versions for all core dependencies (`scipy>=1.13`, `astropy>=6.1`, etc.) to ensure compatibility with NumPy 2.0 or [SPEC 0](https://scientific-python.org/specs/spec-0000/) compliance, whichever was more stringent. Sources for NumPy 2.0 compliance:
        * `scipy`, `astropy`, `h5py`, and `matplotlib`: [numpy/numpy #26191](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/issues/26191)
        * `astro-sedpy`: `v0.4.1` [Release Notes](https://github.com/bd-j/sedpy/releases/tag/v0.4.1)
        * `fsps`: `v0.4.7` [Release Notes](https://github.com/dfm/python-fsps/releases/tag/v0.4.7)
        * `emcee`: [dfm/emcee #515](https://github.com/dfm/emcee/issues/515)
        * `dynesty`: `v2.1.4` [Release Notes](https://github.com/joshspeagle/dynesty/releases/tag/v2.1.4)
        * `corner`: NumPy 2.0 compatibility unknown, but only `v2.2.3` meets [SPEC 0](https://scientific-python.org/specs/spec-0000/) compliance.
* **CI/Test Configuration:**
    * Moved `pytest` configuration into `pyproject.toml` and simplified `.github/workflows/tests.yml` to install dependencies directly from the project metadata.
    * Updated the test matrix to use a min/max strategy:
        * **3.10**: Oldest supported version.
        * **3.14**: Newest stable version.
* **Docs:** Updated `doc/installation.rst` to reflect the new minimum Python requirement.

### Motivation
* **Modernization:** Adopting PEP 621 makes the package compatible with modern tools and simplifies contribution by having a single source of truth for dependencies.
* **Security & Stability:** Python 3.9 and NumPy 1.*x* are no longer receiving security updates.
* **Future Proofing:** Testing against Python 3.14 and enforcing NumPy 2.0 compatible dependencies ensures the package remains robust in modern environments.

### Checklist
- [x] Change support matrix from `3.9, 3.11` to `3.10, 3.14`.
- [x] Implement Fortran compiler fix for `macos-latest` jobs.
- [x] Migrate build system to PEP [621](https://peps.python.org/pep-0621/)/[639](https://peps.python.org/pep-0639/) standards.
- [x] Enforce NumPy 2.0 compatible versions for all dependencies.

case '\\':

Input `Attribute "with quotes"` was exported as `"Attribute \"\with quotes\"\""` instead of `"Attribute \"with quotes\""`.

body:
## Summary

- Adds typed extensions infrastructure enabling formal JSON schemas for vendor-agnostic extension data in `ext.{namespace}` fields
- Implements auto-discovery of extensions during schema build with version filtering via `valid_from`/`valid_until`
- Adds `extensions_supported` field to agent card for declaring typed extension support
- Includes comprehensive test suite for extension infrastructure

## Features

**Extension Meta Schema** (`extension-meta.json`)
- Defines structure all extension files must follow
- `valid_from` (required): Minimum AdCP version (e.g., "2.5")
- `valid_until` (optional): Maximum AdCP version for deprecation

**Auto-Discovery Build System**
- Extensions placed in `/schemas/source/extensions/{namespace}.json` are auto-discovered
- Build script filters extensions by version compatibility for each release
- Registry (`extensions/index.json`) is auto-generated with valid extensions

**Agent Card Extension Support**
- New `extensions_supported` array field in adcp extension
- Agents declare which typed extensions they support
- Enables SDK code generation and schema validation

## How It Works

1. Create extension file at `/schemas/source/extensions/{namespace}.json`
2. Follow the meta schema with `valid_from` specifying minimum AdCP version
3. Build script discovers and includes in appropriate versioned builds
4. Agents declare support via `extensions_supported: ["namespace"]`
5. Clients can validate `ext.{namespace}` data against typed schemas

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm run test:extension-schemas` passes
- [ ] Build script generates extension registry correctly
- [ ] Extension meta schema validates extension structure
- [ ] Agent card accepts `extensions_supported` field
- [ ] Documentation is clear and accurate

## Add IQR-based anomaly detection component

### Description
This pull request introduces a new **IQR-based anomaly detection component** integrated into the RTDIP pipeline framework.

The implementation provides a **modular and reusable anomaly detection solution** that supports both **global** and **rolling IQR** approaches and is designed to operate on generic time-series datasets as well as on **decomposed time-series outputs** (e.g. residual, trend, seasonal components).

### Key Features

- **IQR Anomaly Detection Component**
  - Supports **global IQR** (static thresholds).
  - Supports **rolling IQR** (adaptive, context-aware thresholds).
  - User-configurable sensitivity via parameters (`k`, `window`).

- **Decomposition-Aware Variant**
  - Compatible with the Time Series Decomposition component.
  - Allows anomaly detection on selected components (e.g. residuals).

- **RTDIP Integration**
  - Implemented as a proper RTDIP pipeline component.
  - Config-driven, dataset-agnostic, and reusable.
  - Clean input/output contract preserving the original schema.


### Validation

- The component has been **verified on the Shell dataset**.
- Rolling IQR demonstrates improved detection of contextual anomalies compared to global IQR, which is intentionally conservative in the presence of extreme outliers.

### Scope & Notes

- This PR focuses on **component integration and functionality**.
- Exploratory notebooks and visual analysis results are provided separately under `amos_team_resources`.
- Documentation and references are handled in the corresponding Wiki section.

### Related Work
- Supports integration with Time Series Decomposition.

author: durjoydutta
body:
This pull request introduces user authentication and persistent conversation management to the chat API, along with improvements to streaming chat responses and council deliberation logic. The main changes include enforcing authentication via Supabase JWT tokens, saving and updating chat conversations and messages in the database, and enhancing the streaming endpoint to log metadata and handle errors more robustly.

**Authentication & User Management**
* Added `get_current_user` dependency in `app/api/deps.py` to verify Supabase JWT tokens and extract `user_id` for all chat endpoints.
* All chat endpoints (`/chat`, `/stream`, `/chat/{conversation_id}`) now require authentication and operate with a `user_id`.

**Conversation Persistence & Management**
* Chat requests now create or retrieve conversations and log both user and assistant messages to the database, including metadata such as retrieved chunks and model info. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-37f7b0dfebd5d4dbb8fb6c5d08924862a49be53dbd3fd8659cd6c83e0a5b2290L1-R166) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0362fd50da7ab95f2ceaf921f76d2ab839f7e53f102252e7e4b21b5977c8ce7dR7)
* Added endpoints to delete (`DELETE /chat/{conversation_id}`) and update (`PATCH /chat/{conversation_id}`) conversations, supporting title and pin status changes.
* Streaming chat endpoint logs all events, chunks, and council opinions to the database, with robust error handling and metadata capture.

**Streaming & Council Logic Improvements**
* Streaming responses now include detailed event and metadata logging, and gracefully handle client disconnects and errors by saving partial state.
* Council deliberation logic refactored to classify queries as "LEGAL-ANALYSIS" or "NON-LEGAL" before answering, with strict rules for tagging and response structure.
* Council member models upgraded to newer Gemini versions for improved performance and diversity.
* Council streaming now ensures all async tasks are cancelled if the generator exits early, improving resource management. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-377315c891bac54ff082a58530fa42950b68825fac9a596e11312b11dc4ca974R225) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-377315c891bac54ff082a58530fa42950b68825fac9a596e11312b11dc4ca974R234-R243)

**Configuration & Logging**
* Added Supabase connection settings to `app/config.py` for authentication and database access.
* CORS policy updated to restrict origins to local frontend addresses.
* Request logging now indicates whether authentication is present for improved traceability.

author: kammerdiener
body:
## Summary

This PR contains comprehensive improvements to the Replizieren Kubernetes operator:

- **Bug fixes**: Added missing RBAC markers, fixed error handling, improved namespace parsing
- **Refactoring**: Created shared `replicator.go` module, reducing ~100 lines of duplicate code
- **Testing**: Expanded from 4 tests to 40 tests (24 controller tests + 16 unit tests)
- **CI/CD**: Added GHCR publishing workflow for multi-arch container images

## Changes

### Bug Fixes
- Add missing RBAC markers for ConfigMap controller (was completely missing)
- Add namespace and deployment RBAC permissions to both controllers
- Fix silently ignored errors (`_ = r.Patch(...)`) with proper logging
- Fix namespace parsing edge cases (whitespace trimming, empty string filtering)

### Refactoring
- Create `internal/controller/replicator.go` with shared constants and helpers:
  - `ParseReplicationConfig()` - parse annotations into config struct
  - `GetAllNamespaces()` - list all namespaces except source
  - `RestartDeployments()` - generic deployment restart logic
  - `IsDeploymentUsingSecret()` / `IsDeploymentUsingConfigMap()` - detection helpers

### Testing (40 total tests)
- **Secret controller tests** (12 tests): single namespace, multiple namespaces, all namespaces, skip empty, skip false, update existing, whitespace handling, empty entries, exclude source, trigger rollout, data matches, volume mount rollout
- **ConfigMap controller tests** (12 tests): mirrors Secret tests
- **Unit tests** (16 tests): `ParseReplicationConfig`, `IsDeploymentUsingSecret`, `IsDeploymentUsingConfigMap`

### CI/CD
- New `.github/workflows/publish.yml`:
  - Triggers on version tags (`v*.*.*`)
  - Multi-arch: `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`
  - Auto-generates semver tags: `1.0.0`, `1.0`, `1`
  - Uses GitHub Actions cache for faster builds

> Consolidates replication logic and hardens controllers while adding CI/CD and docs.
> 
> - Refactors controllers to use shared helpers in `internal/controller/replicator.go` (`ParseReplicationConfig`, `GetAllNamespaces`, `RestartDeployments`, detection helpers)
> - Enhances rollout behavior to restart Deployments in both source and target namespaces; replaces silent patches with proper patching
> - Adds missing RBAC markers and expands permissions (namespaces, apps/deployments); updates `config/rbac/role.yaml`
> - Large test expansion: new Ginkgo envtest setup, 24 controller tests for Secrets/ConfigMaps, 16 unit tests for helpers
> - Adds GitHub Actions: `publish.yml` for multi-arch GHCR images on tags; `pages.yml` to build/deploy Jekyll docs
> - Introduces documentation site under `docs/` and updates `README.md` with features, install, and usage

closes #269 

---

### Description
This PR significantly enhances the Dashboard user experience by moving away from static "Coming Soon" text to a dynamic, professional interface. The focus was on improving the "perceived performance" of the app—ensuring that even while data is loading or missing, the interface remains polished and guided.

Beyond the UI, I have also synchronized the backend requirements to ensure a smooth "one-click" setup for future contributors, resolving common dependency issues found in the local development environment.

---

### Changes Made

1. Frontend (UX/UI Refinement):

- Integrated Skeleton Loading: Added custom pulsing placeholders for dashboard metrics and charts. This eliminates jarring layout shifts while waiting for backend responses.
- New Empty State Architecture: Created a reusable EmptyState component with context-aware Lucide icons to replace blank screens on tabs like "Analytics" and "Sponsorships."
- Theme Consistency: Updated Tailwind styles in the DashboardPage to ensure full accessibility and visual parity between light and dark modes.
- Component Modularization: Added Skeleton.tsx and EmptyState.tsx to the UI kit for future use across the application.

2. Backend (Stability & Setup):

- Requirement Alignment: Updated requirements.txt to include essential missing libraries: sqlalchemy, aiopg, and uvicorn.
- Environment Fix: Resolved ModuleNotFoundError issues that previously blocked the FastAPI server from initializing correctly on Windows environments.

body:
## Summary

- Add retry loops (3 attempts with 30-60s delays) to all Maven commands
- Add `-U` flag to force updates and bypass cached failures
- Remove Maven cache from setup-java (caching was contributing to issues)
- Add explicit settings.xml configuration for credentials

## Problem

GitHub Actions runners are intermittently getting 403 Forbidden errors from Maven Central (repo.maven.apache.org). This appears to be rate limiting or IP blocking from Maven Central's side.

## Solution

1. **Retry logic**: Each Maven command now retries up to 3 times with delays between attempts
2. **Force updates**: Added `-U` flag to force Maven to check for updates
3. **No caching**: Removed Maven cache from setup-java action to avoid stale cached data
4. **Explicit settings**: Added settings.xml configuration inline

- [ ] Verify retry logic works on transient failures

author: hra687261
body:
The purpose of this PR is to experiment with using a [modified version](https://github.com/hra687261/landmarks/tree/ocaml5) of the [landmarks library](https://github.com/LexiFi/landmarks) which is intended to work with parallelism.

This modified version comes with the following constraints:
1. Each domain has to run on its own physical core to be able to make proper measures.

    That is done through the [domainPC](https://github.com/hra687261/DomainPC) library which is used as a replacement for the stdlib Domain library. 
    I am not sure if there is a simple way through dune to replace an stdlib module with a another one, maybe we can cheat through an `-open` that would hide the `Domain` of the stdlib?


2. Each domain has to properly exit before the parent domain that spawned it, because `at_exit` is used to aggregate the results of the measurements.
 

The current landmarks that were added are only for testing (and so is this PR btw so its probably not worth merging).

To test this, you can run `OCAML_LANDMARKS=on,allocation dune exec -- owi c doc/src/sap/dobble.c`, which will produce (after owi's output):
```
...
Call graph '/home/hra687261/workspace/wasm/owi_landmarks/_build/install/default/bin/owi c doc/src/sap/dobble.c':
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[    2.32G cycles in  4 calls ]     - 57.07% : Symbolic_choice.CoreImpl.Scheduler.run_worker
[  884.78M cycles in 43 calls ]     |   - 38.18% : Solver.check
[  184.23M cycles in  1 calls ]     |   -  7.95% : Solver.model_of_path_condition
[  798.04M cycles in  1 calls ]     - 19.65% : Cmd_sym.cmd

Note: Nodes accounting for less than 1.00% of their parent have been ignored.

Aggregated table:
----------------
                                         Name;                           Filename;    Calls;     Time; Allocated bytes; Allocated bytes major
                                         ROOT;       src/landmark_state_ocaml5.ml;        0;    4.06G; 122789048; 66476072
Symbolic_choice.CoreImpl.Scheduler.run_worker; src/symbolic/symbolic_choice.ml:95;        4;    2.32G; 10417016; 125256
                                 Solver.check;          src/symbolic/solver.ml:26;       43;  884.78M; 7895576; 55176
                                  Cmd_sym.cmd;              src/cmd/cmd_sym.ml:51;        1;  798.04M; 9972760; 8876200
               Solver.model_of_path_condition;          src/symbolic/solver.ml:30;        1;  184.23M; 536880; 0
                     Interpret.Make.exec_expr;    src/interpret/interpret.ml:1538;        1;    2.16K; 608; 0
```
Notice on the call graph that the sum of the times at the root is not 100% (not yet sure where that time is spent or if that is a measurement error) and that `Symbolic_choice.CoreImpl.Scheduler.run_worker` and `Cmd_sym.cmd` are both at the root, that is because `Cmd_sym.cmd` is run by the main domain while `Symbolic_choice.run_worker` is run by the child domain which makes landmarks see them as "independent" runs. I don't think there is a simple way to stay faithful to the real callgraph, while the time/allocation measurements stay precise for the runs of independent domains.

(cc @redianthus and @bclement-ocp if you want to take a look)

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a lightweight healthcare domain that has comparable complexity to the ATM domain so cross-domain E5 experiments exercise similar difficulty. 
- Make the default E5 runner include both `atm` and `health` domains so the cross-domain experiment works out-of-the-box. 
- Ensure deterministic, offline-friendly runs by using `llm_mode: heuristic` for the included domain configs. 

### Description
- Added healthcare assets: `health_requirements.jsonl`, `gold/health_gold.ttl`, `gold/shapes_health.ttl`, and `health_cqs.rq` and expanded requirements to 30 items to match ATM-level coverage. 
- Added domain configs `configs/health_ontology_aware.json` and `configs/atm_e5_cross_domain.json`, and updated `configs/e5_cross_domain.json` to include both `atm` and `health` domains with appropriate `output_root` entries. 
- Set `llm_mode: "heuristic"` in the domain configs to make runs deterministic and offline-friendly, and added SHACL constraints (including a SPARQL-based no-double-booking constraint) to the health shapes. 
- Updated `README.md` to document the default E5 setup and note that the healthcare assets mirror ATM complexity for comparable cross-domain evaluation. 

### Testing

body:
### Motivation
- The Add Termógrafo flow did not persist per-row `TERMOGRAFO` values to `fruta_exiexportacion.N_TERMOGRAFO` when pressing the add button. 
- Nested/per-row forms and inconsistent submit flags caused the detail inputs to be omitted or overwritten during `QUITAR` and other actions. 
- Each termógrafo must be associated with the specific folio row (`ID_EXIEXPORTACION`) where it was entered. 
- Make the add-button behavior explicit and avoid relying on implicit form/button `form` attributes for reliability across browsers. 

### Description
- Replace per-row nested forms and the `IDTERMOGRAFO[]` counter by wrapping all detail rows in a single `form-termografos` and keeping per-row hidden inputs `IDDESPACHO[]`, `FOLIOEXIEXPORTACIONTERMOGRAFO[]`, and `IDEXIEXPORTACIONTERMOGRAFO[]`. 
- Change the Add button to call a new JS helper `submitTermografosForm()` which injects a hidden `TERMOGRAFOS` input and submits `form-termografos`, preventing `TERMOGRAFOS` from being submitted during `QUITAR` actions. 
- Add server-side helper `actualizarTermografosDespacho($EXIEXPORTACION_ADO, $EXIEXPORTACION, $request)` that iterates `IDEXIEXPORTACIONTERMOGRAFO[]`/`TERMOGRAFO[]`, skips empty values, sets `ID_DESPACHO`, `ID_EXIEXPORTACION`, `N_TERMOGRAFO` and calls `actualizarDespachoAgregarTermografo()`, and invoke it from `CREAR`, `GUARDAR`, `CERRAR` and the `TERMOGRAFOS` handler. 
- Convert per-row `QUITAR` to a single submit button that sends the row id as the button `value`, and remove stray SQL debug `echo` from `actualizarDespachoAgregarTermografo`. 

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for this change. 
- The change was committed and the relevant file modified was `fruta/vista/registroDespachoEX.php`. 
- Server-side update uses existing `EXIEXPORTACION_ADO::actualizarDespachoAgregarTermografo()` which was left intact and is invoked by the new helper.

# What does this PR do?

This PR switches to use `asyncio.run` instead of `asyncio.get_event_loop()` + `result = loop.run_until_complete()`. This is better as starting from python3.14, `get_event_loop` returns a `RuntimeError` if there is no loop. Before, it was creating a loop if it didn't exist. 

Fixes https://github.com/huggingface/accelerate/issues/3899

author: carlosvale03
body:
## Descrição
Refatoração completa do fluxo de Cartão de Crédito para atender aos requisitos de contabilidade e UX do Frontend. Despesas agora nascem como "Pendentes" e só afetam o saldo da conta após o pagamento da fatura.

## Mudanças Principais

### 1. Refatoração de Despesas (`PENDING`)
- **Model**: Adicionado campo `status` ('PENDING', 'COMPLETED') em `Transaction`.
- **Lógica**: Novas despesas de cartão (`POST /credit-card-expense/`) são criadas como `PENDING` e vinculadas à conta do cartão. Elas NÃO não descontam do saldo da conta bancária até serem pagas.

### 2. Pagamento de Fatura (`/pay`)
- **Lógica Renovada**: Ao pagar uma fatura (Total ou Parcial), o sistema NÃO cria mais uma transação duplicada de "Pagamento".
- **Comportamento**: Ele busca as transações originais da fatura e:
    - Atualiza status para `COMPLETED`.
    - Atualiza a conta para a conta pagadora (Checking/Savings).
    - Atualiza a data para o dia do pagamento.
- **Rollover Automático**: Em pagamentos parciais, o saldo devedor (transações não pagas) é movido automaticamente para a fatura do mês seguinte.

### 3. Estorno de Fatura (`/unpay`)
- **Novo Endpoint**: `POST /api/invoices/{id}/unpay/`
- **Funcionalidade**: Reverte um pagamento de fatura, voltando as transações para `PENDING` e restaurando o status da fatura para `OPEN`. Isso corrige o saldo da conta imediatamente.

### 4. Ajustes no Serializer
- Adicionado `account_detail` (id, name) no `TransactionSerializer` para facilitar a exibição no Frontend.

## Testes
- Validação via script `verify_refactor.py` cobrindo fluxos de:
    - Compra Parcelada.
    - Pagamento Total (Validação de saldo e status).
    - Pagamento Parcial (Validação de rollover).
    - Estorno (Validação de reversão de status e saldo).

body:
Previously, Map type expectations returned raw tuple rows, which broke downstream parsing when `unexpected_rows` were included in validation results. This change introduces a new opt-in flag `map_expectation_unexpected_rows_as_dict` to Chekpoint config to ensure all map expectations `unexpected_rows` are serialized as dictionaries for sqlachemy and spark (pandas already return serializable dataframes).
The default format output is unchanged (strigified tuple of row values)

Default format: `(1.0, 1.0, 2.0)`
Serialized format (with `map_expectation_unexpected_rows_as_dict=True`):  `{"col_a": 1.0, "col_b": 1.0, "col_c": 2.0}`

### Motivation

- Updated `app.js` to wire the new buttons and behavior: `goToPreviousLevel()` decrements `activeLevelIndex` and calls `renderLevel()`, and `goToNextLevel()` unlocks the next level if needed (increments `unlockedLevels`, calls `saveProgress()`), sets `activeLevelIndex` to the next index, and refreshes the UI via `renderLevelList()` + `renderLevel()`.
- Added mobile menu state and handlers: `openMobileMenu()`, `closeMobileMenu()`, a click-to-close overlay, auto-closing the drawer when selecting a level, and a `resize` listener to restore sidebar behavior on larger screens.
- Kept progress updates and disabling of navigation buttons in `renderLevel()` so UI state remains consistent with `unlockedLevels` and `activeLevelIndex`.

author: macmayo1993
body:
## Core Implementation

- **MDL module** (core/mdl.py): Rigorous bit-based MDL calculations with Rissanen's normalized maximum likelihood
- **Orientation tracking** (core/orientation.py): OrientationTracker class for navigating quotient space ℂᴺ/ℤ₂
- **Flip atoms** (core/flip_atoms.py): FlipAtom base class with SignFlip, TimeReversal, VarianceScale, PolynomialDetrend implementations
- **Seam detection** (core/seam_detection.py): Roughness-based detection with CUSUM and Bayesian changepoint methods

## Theory Module

- **k* constant** (theory/k_star.py): Compute k* = 1/(2·ln 2) ≈ 0.721 with Monte Carlo validation
- Validates theoretical phase boundary emergence from MDL, not empirical fitting

## Models

- **MASS framework** (models/mass_framework.py): Manifold-Aware Seam Segmentation with greedy seam addition
- **Baselines** (models/baselines.py): Polynomial, Fourier, AR, and Constant baselines for comparison

## Utilities

- **Synthetic data** (utils/synthetic_data.py): Generate benchmark signals with known seams (sign flip, variance shift, HVAC-like)

## Testing

- **k* convergence test**: Monte Carlo validation that k* emerges from theory
- **MDL tests**: Validate bit counting, monotonicity, parameter penalties
- **Flip atom tests**: Verify involution properties and correctness

## Documentation

- **README.md**: Public-facing overview with quick examples
- **THEORY.md**: Rigorous mathematical foundations with full derivations
- **ARCHITECTURE.md**: Software design principles and extension points
- **LICENSE**: Apache 2.0
- **CONTRIBUTING.md**: Development guidelines

## CI/CD

- GitHub Actions workflow for Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11
- Automated testing with pytest and coverage
- Code quality checks (black, isort, flake8)

This represents a complete, production-ready framework for seam-aware time series analysis based on non-orientable manifold theory.

# Improve CLI initialization and add new agents

## 📋 Summary

This PR enhances the CLI initialization experience by adding interactive prompts for language and Primary Agent selection, introduces three new specialized agents (data-engineer, mobile-developer, i18n-specialist), and significantly improves agent resolution logic with pattern matching and context-based inference.

## 🎯 Motivation

- **Better Onboarding**: Interactive prompts make CLI initialization more user-friendly and reduce configuration errors
- **Specialized Expertise**: New agents provide domain-specific knowledge for database, mobile, and internationalization tasks
- **Smarter Agent Selection**: Improved pattern matching and context inference ensure the right agent is selected automatically
- **Consistency**: Centralized language and agent display information ensures consistent UI/CLI experience

## 🔧 Key Changes

### 1. CLI Initialization Improvements

#### Language Selection Prompt
- Added `language-prompt.ts` with interactive language selection
- Supports Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese, and Spanish
- Uses centralized `SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES` from `keyword.types.ts`
- Defaults to Korean (`ko`) for consistency

#### Primary Agent Selection Prompt
- Added `agent-prompt.ts` with interactive Primary Agent selection
- Displays human-readable agent names and descriptions
- Uses `ACT_AGENT_DISPLAY_INFO` for consistent formatting
- Defaults to `frontend-developer` for backward compatibility

#### Template Renderer Updates
- Added `primaryAgent` option to `TemplateRenderOptions`
- Updated renderer to include `primaryAgent` in generated config files
- Supports both `defaultModel` and `primaryAgent` in AI configuration section

### 2. New Specialized Agents

#### Data Engineer (`data-engineer.json`)
- **Expertise**: Database design, schema migrations, query optimization, ERD design
- **Activation Patterns**: 
  - Files: `.sql`, `schema.prisma`, `migrations/`, `.entity.ts`
  - Keywords: "데이터베이스", "스키마", "migration", "ERD", "쿼리 최적화"
- **Use Cases**: Database schema design, migration scripts, query optimization, data modeling

#### Mobile Developer (`mobile-developer.json`)
- **Expertise**: React Native, Flutter, iOS (Swift/SwiftUI), Android (Kotlin/Compose)
- **Activation Patterns**:
  - Files: `react-native.config.js`, `metro.config.js`, `pubspec.yaml`, `.dart`, `.swift`, `.kt`, `Podfile`, `AndroidManifest.xml`
  - Keywords: "모바일", "React Native", "Flutter", "iOS", "Android"
- **Use Cases**: Mobile app development, cross-platform frameworks, native mobile development
- **Platform Support**: Cross-platform (React Native, Flutter) and native (iOS, Android)

#### i18n Specialist (`i18n-specialist.json`)
- **Expertise**: Internationalization, localization, translation management, RTL support
- **Activation Patterns**: i18n-related tasks, translation files, locale configuration
- **Use Cases**: Multi-language support, translation key management, locale-specific formatting, RTL layout

### 3. Enhanced Agent Resolution Logic

#### Pattern Matching Improvements
- Added `DATA_INTENT_PATTERNS` for data-engineer detection
- Added `MOBILE_INTENT_PATTERNS` for mobile-developer detection
- Supports both English and Korean keywords
- Confidence levels: 0.85-0.98 based on pattern specificity

#### Context-Based Resolution
- **Mobile Context Patterns**: Detects mobile projects from file paths
  - React Native: `react-native.config.js`, `metro.config.js`, `app.json`
  - Flutter: `pubspec.yaml`, `.dart` files
  - iOS: `.swift`, `Podfile`, `.xcodeproj`
  - Android: `.kt`, `AndroidManifest.xml`, `build.gradle`
- **Data Context Patterns**: Detects database-related files
  - SQL files, Prisma schema, migration directories, entity files
- **Project Type Context**: Infrastructure project type detection

#### Resolution Priority Order
Updated ACT mode resolution priority:
1. Explicit agent request in prompt
2. `recommended_agent` parameter (from PLAN mode)
3. Tooling intent patterns (config files)
4. **Data intent patterns** (database/schema tasks)
5. **Mobile intent patterns** (mobile app tasks)
6. Project configuration
7. Context inference (file paths/extensions)
8. Default fallback

### 4. Type System Enhancements

#### Language Display Information
- Added `SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES` constant with display names and descriptions
- Added `LanguageDisplayInfo` interface
- Added `DEFAULT_LANGUAGE_CODE` and `SUPPORTED_LANGUAGE_CODES` constants
- Centralized language information for CLI and UI consistency

#### Agent Display Information
- Added `ACT_AGENT_DISPLAY_INFO` constant with human-readable names and descriptions
- Added `AgentDisplayInfo` interface
- Provides consistent formatting across CLI prompts and UI

### 5. API Design Skill Documentation
- Added comprehensive `api-design` skill documentation
- Covers REST and GraphQL API design patterns
- Includes OpenAPI specification examples
- Documents versioning strategies, error handling, and best practices

## ⚠️ Breaking Changes

None. All changes are backward compatible.

## 📌 Migration Guide

### For CLI Users

The CLI `init` command now includes interactive prompts:

```bash
# Before: Manual configuration editing required
codingbuddy init

# After: Interactive prompts guide you through setup
codingbuddy init
# → Select response language: [Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese, Spanish]
# → Select your primary development agent: [Tooling Engineer, Data Engineer, ...]
```

### For Agent Resolution

New agents are automatically detected based on:
- **File context**: Working with mobile/data files triggers appropriate agent
- **Prompt keywords**: Using domain-specific terms selects the right agent
- **Project type**: Infrastructure projects suggest devops-engineer

No manual configuration needed - the system intelligently selects agents.

## ✅ Testing

- Added comprehensive test coverage for language and agent prompts
- Added pattern matching tests for data-engineer and mobile-developer
- Added context-based resolution tests for mobile and data file patterns
- All existing tests pass with new agent additions
- Template renderer tests updated for primaryAgent support

## 🔍 Review Checklist

- [ ] CLI prompts work correctly for language and agent selection
- [ ] New agents are properly activated based on patterns and context
- [ ] Agent resolution priority order is correct
- [ ] Template renderer correctly includes primaryAgent in config files
- [ ] Language and agent display info is consistent across CLI/UI
- [ ] Pattern matching covers common use cases
- [ ] Context-based resolution works for mobile and data projects
- [ ] No breaking changes to existing functionality
- [ ] Documentation is clear and comprehensive

---

Closes #151

body:
The `TestMetrics` tests are failing on my machine's and Luit's, as the Minio Go SDK seems to issue different errors on macOS (a difference in resolving?).

That prompted me to rewrite the tests to make sure the use of a healthy backend sees no metrics being collected, and test that metrics are collected with an error we have more control over.

Moreover, working on this made me realise that we collect `ErrNotExist` just as other errors. Since it does not reflect an unhealthy backend but merely a missing key, I also propose we no longer collect it.

Lastly, we no longer return `ErrNotExist` for a missing bucket, as it is a completely different error.

Remove the SearchReleases RPC and related digest lookup functionality that was used to avoid creating duplicate releases. The system will now always create new releases without checking for duplicates by digest.

- Remove `SearchReleases` RPC from `release_service.proto`
- Remove `SearchReleasesRequest` and `SearchReleasesResponse` message types

- The digest field remains in the database and in the `ReleaseMessage` struct, but is no longer used for filtering/searching

## 📝 개요 (Description)

백엔드 애플리케이션의 데이터 영속성을 위한 TypeORM 및 PostgreSQL 설정을 완료했습니다.

PostgreSQL 18.1 공식 이미지를 사용하여 Docker Compose로 데이터베이스 환경을 구성했으며, TypeORM의 synchronize 기능을 통해 개발 환경에서 자동으로 테이블이 생성되도록 설정했습니다. 모든 Entity는 PostgreSQL 호환 데이터 타입(timestamp, jsonb, enum, bigint)을 사용하여 구현했습니다.

## 🔗 관련 이슈 (Related Issues)
-   Closes #56

## 🏷️ 작업 유형 (Type of Change)
-   [x] ✨ 기능 추가 (New Feature)
-   [ ] 🐛 버그 수정 (Bug Fix)
-   [ ] ♻️ 리팩토링 (Refactoring)
-   [ ] 📝 문서 업데이트 (Documentation)
-   [x] 🔧 설정 변경 및 기타 (Config & Other)

## ✅ 체크리스트 (Checklist)
-   [x] 코드가 정상적으로 컴파일/빌드 되나요?
-   [x] 기존 테스트를 통과했나요? (새로운 테스트가 필요하다면 추가했나요?)
-   [x] 스스로 코드를 리뷰했나요? (Self-review)
-   [x] 불필요한 주석이나 디버깅 코드는 제거했나요?
-   [x] 문서(README 등)에 변경 사항을 업데이트했나요?

## 📸 스크린샷 (Screenshots)

![img](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/367a9156-552f-4c25-9a62-59d11fe84d3b)

## 🎸 기타 (Etc)

### 🛠 주요 변경 사항

#### 1. 패키지 설치
- `@nestjs/typeorm`, `typeorm`, `pg`: TypeORM 및 PostgreSQL 드라이버
- `@nestjs/config`: 환경변수 관리

#### 2. PostgreSQL 설정 (docker-compose.yml)
- PostgreSQL 18.1 공식 이미지 사용
- Health check 설정으로 안정적인 컨테이너 시작 보장
- 볼륨 마운트 경로: `/var/lib/postgresql` (PostgreSQL 18+ 호환)
- 데이터 영속성을 위한 `postgres_data` 볼륨 추가

#### 3. TypeORM 설정 (app.module.ts)
- `TypeOrmModule.forRootAsync`로 비동기 설정
- 로컬 개발 및 Docker 환경 모두 지원하는 envFilePath 설정
- Entity 자동 로딩: `__dirname + '/**/*.entity{.ts,.js}'`
- 개발 환경에서만 `synchronize: true` (자동 테이블 생성)
- 개발 모드에서 SQL 로깅 활성화

#### 4. Entity 생성 (11개)
**User 모듈**
- `User`: 사용자 기본 정보 및 OAuth 인증
- `UserStatistics`: 사용자 통계 (승/패, 티어 포인트, 경험치)

**Tier 모듈**
- `Tier`: 티어 정보 (이름, 포인트 범위, 아이콘)
- `UserTierHistory`: 사용자 티어 변경 이력

**Question 모듈**
- `Question`: 문제 정보 (타입, 내용, 정답, 난이도)
- `Category`: 카테고리 (계층 구조 지원)
- `CategoryQuestion`: 문제-카테고리 다대다 관계

**Match 모듈**
- `Match`: 매치 정보 (싱글/멀티, 플레이어, 승자)
- `Round`: 라운드 정보 (매치별 문제)
- `RoundAnswer`: 라운드별 답안 및 채점 결과 (grading_criteria, grading_details 포함)

**Problem Bank 모듈**
- `UserProblemBank`: 사용자별 문제 은행 (북마크, 답안, 피드백)

#### 5. 모듈 구조 재배치
```
src/
├── user/          (user.entity.ts, user-statistics.entity.ts)
├── tier/          (tier.entity.ts, user-tier-history.entity.ts)
├── quiz/      (question.entity.ts, category.entity.ts, category-question.entity.ts)
├── match/         (match.entity.ts, round.entity.ts, round-answer.entity.ts)
└── problem-bank/  (user-problem-bank.entity.ts)
```

#### 6. PostgreSQL 호환성
- `datetime` → `timestamp` (PostgreSQL 표준)
- `Record<string, any>` → `Record<string, unknown>` (TypeScript best practice)
- `jsonb` 타입 사용 (grading_criteria, grading_details)
- `bigint` 타입으로 모든 ID 통일

#### 7. 환경변수 통합
- `POSTGRES_*`와 `DB_*` 변수를 `DB_*`로 일원화
- `.env.example`에 DB 설정 추가
- 로컬/Docker 환경 모두 지원

### ✨ 개발 환경 실행 방법
```bash
# PostgreSQL 시작
docker compose up -d postgres

# 백엔드 실행 (TypeORM이 자동으로 테이블 생성)
cd packages/backend
pnpm dev

# 테이블 생성 확인
docker compose exec postgres psql -U web05_user -d web05_db -c "\dt"
```

Establishes a complete course repository structure for teaching linear regression with emphasis on reproducibility, following Fox's *Applied Regression Analysis* pedagogy and tidyverse conventions.

## Structure

- **data/** - Sample datasets with data dictionaries (student performance CSV with 7 variables)
- **lectures/** - R Markdown lecture materials (01-introduction.Rmd covers reproducibility fundamentals)
- **vignettes/** - Extended tutorials (reproducible-analysis-template.Rmd provides reusable workflow)
- **shiny/** - Interactive apps (simple-regression-app for parameter exploration)

## Documentation

- **README.md** - Course philosophy, installation, tidyverse setup, Fox textbook alignment
- **AI-DISCLAIMER.md** - AI tool usage policy, permitted/prohibited uses, academic integrity
- **QUICKSTART.md** - Setup guide with troubleshooting
- **CONTRIBUTING.md** - Student contribution guidelines
- **setup.R** - Automated package installation script

## Technical Approach

All examples use tidyverse ecosystem (`dplyr`, `ggplot2`, `broom`) with consistent style:

```r
# Load and explore data
data <- read_csv("data/student_performance.csv")

# Fit model with tidy output
model <- lm(test_score ~ hours_studied + attendance_rate, data = data)
tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE)

# Visualize with ggplot2
ggplot(data, aes(x = hours_studied, y = test_score)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")
```

Each folder contains detailed README with templates, best practices, and quality checklists. R-specific .gitignore excludes build artifacts and package libraries.

author: swannysec
body:
## Summary

Fixes an issue where the scorecard fails to render for Google's privacy policy while working correctly for Microsoft's policy.

## Root Cause

The original regex-based JSON extraction (`/\{[\s\S]*\}/`) was greedy and would capture invalid JSON when the LLM included extra text before or after the JSON object (e.g., "Here's the analysis: {...} Note: ...").

## Solution

Replaced regex-based extraction with character-by-character parsing that:
1. Tracks brace/bracket depth properly
2. Handles string escaping correctly
3. Tries multiple extraction strategies until one succeeds
4. Falls back gracefully on parse failures

## Security Improvements

After code and security review, additional hardening was added:

| Protection | Implementation |
|------------|----------------|
| ReDoS prevention | Character-by-character parsing (O(n) complexity) |
| Memory exhaustion | `MAX_ARRAY_ITEMS = 100` limit on parsed arrays |
| Field size limits | `MAX_FIELD_LENGTH = 10000` chars per field |
| Consistent sanitization | All parsers now clean markdown code blocks |

## Changes

- **`src/services/analysis/ResponseParser.ts`**
  - Add `extractJsonObject<T>()` - robust JSON object extraction
  - Add `extractJsonArray<T>()` - robust JSON array extraction  
  - Add `cleanMarkdownCodeBlocks()` helper
  - Add `MAX_ARRAY_ITEMS` and `MAX_FIELD_LENGTH` constants
  - Update `parseScorecard()`, `parsePrivacyRights()`, `parseRisks()`, `parseKeyTerms()` to use new methods

## Testing

- All 568 tests pass
- Build succeeds
- Manual testing recommended with Google's privacy policy

## Security Review

Reviewed for:
- [x] ReDoS vulnerabilities (eliminated)
- [x] Memory exhaustion attacks (mitigated with limits)
- [x] Infinite loop potential (bounded by string length)
- [x] XSS (React auto-escapes; no innerHTML usage)

body:
## Summary

- Consolidate all sensitive data sanitization into the `privacy` package
- Add semantic logger field constructors for type-safe sensitive data logging
- Remove duplicate sanitization code (~80 lines from workers.go)
- Add linter rules to catch unsafe logging patterns

## Changes

### New Privacy Functions
- `ScrubUsername()` - hash username for safe log correlation
- `ScrubPassword()` - complete redaction
- `ScrubToken()` - redact with length hint for debugging
- `ScrubCredentialURL()` - sanitize notification service URLs
- `WrapError()` - wrap errors with sanitized messages

### New Logger Field Constructors
- `logger.Username(value)` - hashes username
- `logger.Password(value)` - always `[REDACTED]`
- `logger.Token(key, value)` - shows `[TOKEN:len=N]`
- `logger.URL(key, value)` - sanitizes URLs
- `logger.CredentialURL(key, value)` - sanitizes credential URLs
- `logger.SanitizedString(key, value)` - full privacy scrubbing
- `logger.SanitizedError(err)` - scrubs error messages
- `logger.Credential(key)` - marks as `[REDACTED]`

### Code Cleanup
- Updated 12 auth logging locations to use `logger.Username()`
- Updated MQTT client to use `logger.Username()`
- Updated notification services to use `privacy.WrapError()`
- Renamed `sanitizeString` to `stringOrDefault` in sound_level.go

### Lint Rules
Added `forbidigo` rules to warn when `logger.String()` is used with sensitive field names like `password`, `token`, `username`, `email`.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test -race ./internal/privacy/...` - All tests pass
- [x] `go test -race ./internal/logger/...` - All tests pass

author: nimmanagotitharunkumarhello
body:
Overview

This PR replaces the existing manual session-based authentication (session['user_id']) with Flask-Login, providing a secure, standardized, and production-ready authentication flow.

Key Changes

Integrated Flask-Login for session management.

Initialized LoginManager in the app factory (backend/__init__.py).

Registered a centralized user_loader to restore authenticated users from the session.

Updated the User model to inherit from UserMixin.

Refactored /login to support GET (render login form) and POST (authenticate user).

Implemented /logout using logout_user() to safely clear sessions.

Protected /profile using the @login_required decorator.

Added safe handling for the next parameter to prevent open redirect vulnerabilities.

Deprecated /auth and added a 302 redirect to /login to maintain a single authentication entry point.

Unauthorized Access & Redirect Handling

When an unauthenticated user accesses a protected route (e.g. /profile), Flask-Login intercepts the request and redirects the user to /login.

The originally requested URL is preserved via the next query parameter.

After successful authentication, users are redirected back to the intended route only if the URL is validated as safe.

Session Persistence

On successful login, Flask-Login stores the user ID in Flask’s signed session cookie.

On subsequent requests, the registered user_loader retrieves the user from the database.

The authenticated user is exposed via the current_user proxy throughout the request lifecycle.

Verification Plan

Manual Testing

Visit /profile while logged out → redirected to /login

Log in with valid credentials → redirected to /profile

Access /profile after refresh → session persists

Log out → redirected to /login

Attempt /profile again → access denied and redirected

Notes

All manual session checks have been removed.

No database files were included in this PR.

Authentication logic is now centralized and aligned with Flask-Login best practices.

Closes #129

author: tolik0
body:
## What
<!--
* Describe what the change is solving. Link all GitHub issues related to this change.
-->
Resolves: https://github.com/airbytehq/oncall/issues/8346

Fixes API errors in source-intercom caused by duplicate concurrent requests to the companies scroll endpoint. The Intercom API only allows one scroll open per app at a time. When `companies` was read both as a standalone stream and as a parent stream for substreams (like `company_segments`), simultaneous API calls caused `400 - scroll already exists` errors.

This PR makes two complementary changes:
1. **Prevents concurrent reads** — serializes access to the companies endpoint so only one read runs at a time
2. **Retries scroll conflicts** — if a 400 scroll error still occurs (e.g., from external scroll usage), the connector now retries with a 60-second backoff instead of failing immediately

## How
<!--
* Describe how code changes achieve the solution.
-->

### 1. Block simultaneous syncs via `stream_groups` (manifest.yaml)

Added a `stream_groups` configuration with `BlockSimultaneousSyncsAction` for the companies stream. This uses a new CDK feature (introduced in https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte-python-cdk/pull/870) that prevents streams in the same group from running concurrently.

```yaml
stream_groups:
  companies_group:
    streams:
      - $ref: "#/definitions/streams/companies"
    action:
      type: BlockSimultaneousSyncsAction
```

### 2. Retry scroll 400 errors with backoff (manifest.yaml)

Changed the companies endpoint error handler for HTTP 400 (`scroll already exists`) from `action: FAIL` to `action: RETRY` with a `ConstantBackoffStrategy` of 60 seconds (matching the Intercom scroll expiry time).

### 3. Dev CDK pinning (metadata.yaml, poe_tasks.toml, unit_tests/)

The `stream_groups` + `BlockSimultaneousSyncsAction` feature is not yet available in a stable CDK release. The connector pins to dev CDK version `7.6.1.post28.dev22724700845` via:
- Base image in `metadata.yaml`
- CDK CLI override in new `poe_tasks.toml`
- Test dependency in `unit_tests/pyproject.toml`

### 4. Troubleshooting documentation (docs/integrations/sources/intercom.md)

Added a "Troubleshooting and limitations" section documenting:
- Client-side incremental sync behavior for Companies/Company Segments (API doesn't support datetime filtering)
- Single scroll per app limitation
- Recommendation to sync these streams in separate connections to avoid long sync times

## Review guide
<!--
1. `x.py`
2. `y.py`
-->
1. `manifest.yaml` — Core changes: `stream_groups` config (top of file) and error handler changes (companies stream `error_handler` section)
2. `metadata.yaml` — Base image and version bump
3. `poe_tasks.toml` — New file, pins CDK CLI to dev version
4. `unit_tests/pyproject.toml` + `poetry.lock` — CDK test dependency pinned
5. `docs/integrations/sources/intercom.md` — New troubleshooting section + changelog

### Human review checklist

- [ ] **Dev CDK dependency**: Confirm that pinning to dev CDK version `7.6.1.post28.dev22724700845` is acceptable for production deployment
- [ ] **60-second backoff**: Verify that 60 seconds is the correct backoff time for scroll conflicts (matches scroll expiry)
- [ ] **Behavioral change**: Confirm that retrying scroll 400 errors (instead of failing immediately) is the desired behavior

## User Impact
<!--
* What is the end result perceived by the user?
* If there are negative side effects, please list them. 
-->

**Positive:**
- Users syncing both `companies` and `company_segments` will no longer experience `400 - scroll already exists` errors
- If scroll conflicts still occur (e.g., from external usage), the connector will retry automatically instead of failing

**Potential side effects:**
- Syncs may take longer if frequent scroll conflicts occur (up to 60 seconds per retry)
- For large workspaces, the client-side incremental sync behavior (documented in troubleshooting) means full dataset reads are required to filter recent records

## Can this PR be safely reverted and rolled back?
<!--
* If unsure, leave it blank.
-->
- [x] YES 💚

The dev CDK dependency is backward-compatible. Reverting would remove the `stream_groups` config, causing the connector to revert to previous behavior (simultaneous reads, immediate failure on scroll 400 errors). Existing connections will continue to work.

---

author: tbroadley
body:
## This PR contains:
- [ ] New features
- [ ] Changes to dev-tools e.g. CI config / github tooling
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Bug fixes
- [ ] Code refactor

### What is the current behavior? (You can also link to an open issue here)

I noticed some unexpected behaviour in the `answer(pattern="line")` scorer. If the solver's completion contains a string like "answer: ...", the scanner returns that as the answer, even if the last line of the completion also contains "ANSWER: ..."

E.g. if the completion looks like:

```
...

  - True answer: only chapter 2 remains ⇒ 1.

...

ANSWER: A
```

`answer` will treat "only chapter 2 remains ⇒ 1." as the solver's answer.

`answer(pattern="letter")` and `answer(pattern="word")` have similar behaviour, where if `answer: a` or `answer: abc` appears at the end of a line in the solver output, then that'll be treated as the answer. I'm not changing that behaviour in this PR because it seems less likely to cause weird behaviour. But, maybe it is worth changing all the same?

Also, `llm_scanner` in Inspect Scout has the same unexpected behaviour. That's how I discovered this behaviour originally.

### What is the new behavior?

`ANSWER_PATTERN_LINE` now only matches `answer: ...` text that is right at the end of the model's output (except for trailing whitespace).

### Does this PR introduce a breaking change? (What changes might users need to make in their application due to this PR?)

This does change the behaviour of `answer` in ways that will probably affect a bunch of existing tasks. I would argue it's a bugfix, but I think it's also fair to see it as a breaking change.

### Other information:

author: copilot
body:
WASM build was failing due to unexpected `cfg` condition warnings treated as errors. Additionally, the demo was silently falling back to precompiled IR files on compilation failures.

## Changes

**Cargo.toml** - Declare WASM dependencies as optional features
```toml
[target.'cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")'.dependencies]
console_error_panic_hook = { version = "0.1", optional = true }
wee_alloc = { version = "0.4", optional = true }

[features]
default = ["console_error_panic_hook", "wee_alloc"]
console_error_panic_hook = ["dep:console_error_panic_hook"]
wee_alloc = ["dep:wee_alloc"]
```

This resolves the mismatch where `wasm.rs` checks `#[cfg(feature = "...")]` but features weren't declared.

**rpg-demo.html** - Remove IR file fallback mechanism
```javascript
async function loadScenarioIR(scenarioId) {
  // Compile from source files - fail fast if compilation fails
  if (typeof BlinkCompiler === 'undefined' || !BlinkCompiler.compile) {
    throw new Error('BlinkCompiler is not available. Cannot compile scenario from source.');
  }
  return await compileScenario(scenarioId);
}
```

Removed the 30+ line fallback loop that tried loading precompiled IR from multiple paths.

**Makefile** - Fix bundle copy paths
The engine bundle is built directly to `game/demos/`, not `packages/blink-engine/dist/`, so removed the redundant copy command.

author: copilot
body:
Implements basic MPI domain decomposition across ranks to enable parallel execution. Phase 2 deliberately omits inter-rank communication—particles leaving domain boundaries are removed and field discontinuities at boundaries are expected.

## Changes

**Simulation structure (`simulation.h`, `simulation.c`)**
- Added MPI topology fields to `t_simulation`: `rank`, `size`, `neighbor_left`, `neighbor_right`
- Updated `sim_new()` signature to accept and store MPI parameters
- Modified `sim_iter()` to remove out-of-bounds particles instead of migrating:

```c
// Phase 2: Simply remove particles leaving domain (no migration)
for (int i = 0; i < sim->n_species; i++) {
    t_species* spec = &sim->species[i];
    int new_np = 0;
    for (int j = 0; j < spec->np; j++) {
        if (spec->part[j].ix >= 0 && spec->part[j].ix < spec->nx) {
            spec->part[new_np++] = spec->part[j];
        }
    }
    spec->np = new_np;
}
// NO field exchange - Phase 2 has no communication
```

**Input configuration (`input/laser_particles.c`)**
- Simplified density profile to `UNIFORM` across all ranks (was `STEP` at global position 54.0, beyond simulation box)
- Fixed laser positioning to correctly map global coordinates to rank-local coordinates

**Error handling (`main.c`)**
- Changed energy conservation check from exit(1) to warning (broken energy conservation is expected without communication)
- Added `ENERGY_CHANGE_THRESHOLD` constant

## Expected Behavior
- Speedup through parallel execution on proper MPI hardware
- Energy not conserved (no field/current exchange between ranks)
- Particle loss at domain boundaries (no migration)
