<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 
> # Phase 2: MPI Domain Decomposition
> 
> Implement basic domain decomposition across MPI ranks WITHOUT inter-rank communication. This phase focuses on **speedup through parallelism**, accepting that physics at domain boundaries will be incorrect.
> 
> ## Changes Needed:
> 
> ### 1. **simulation.h** - Add MPI fields to t_simulation struct
> 
> Around line 40, add to `typedef struct Simulation`:
> ```c
> // MPI parallel info
> int rank;          
> int size;          
> int neighbor_left;  
> int neighbor_right; 
> ```
> 
> Update `sim_new()` declaration:
> ```c
> void sim_new( t_simulation* sim, int nx, float box, float dt, float tmax, int ndump, 
>               t_species* species, int n_species, int rank, int size );
> ```
> 
> ### 2. **simulation.c** - Update for MPI (no communication)
> 
> - Add `#include <mpi.h>` at top
> - Update `sim_new()` to accept and store `rank` and `size`
> - Set `neighbor_left` and `neighbor_right` for topology
> - In `sim_iter()`: Remove particles at domain boundaries (no migration yet)
> 
> Key principle: **Each rank runs independently, particles disappearing at edges is OK for Phase 2**
> 
> ```c
> void sim_iter( t_simulation* sim ) {
>     // Advance particles and deposit current
>     current_zero( &sim -> current );
>     for (int i = 0; i<sim -> n_species; i++)
>         spec_advance(&sim -> species[i], &sim -> emf, &sim -> current );
> 
>     // Phase 2: Simply remove particles leaving domain (no migration)
>     for (int i = 0; i < sim->n_species; i++) {
>         t_species* spec = &sim->species[i];
>         int new_np = 0;
>         for (int j = 0; j < spec->np; j++) {
>             // Keep only particles with valid cell index
>             if (spec->part[j].ix >= 0 && spec->part[j].ix < spec->nx) {
>                 spec->part[new_np++] = spec->part[j];
>             }
>         }
>         spec->np = new_np;
>     }
> 
>     // Update current boundary conditions
>     current_update( &sim -> current );
> 
>     // Advance EM fields
>     emf_advance( &sim -> emf, &sim -> current );
>     
>     // NO field exchange - Phase 2 has no communication
> }
> ```
> 
> ### 3. **input/laser_particles.c** - Domain decomposition logic
> 
> Update `sim_init()` signature:
> ```c
> void sim_init( t_simulation* sim, int rank, int size )
> ```
> 
> Split the 20,000 cell domain:
> ```c
> // Global simulation box
> int nx_global = 20000;
> float box_global = 20.0;
> 
> // Local domain per rank
> int nx_local = nx_global / size;
> float box_local = box_global / size;
> 
> // Calculate local box boundaries
> float local_box_start = rank * box_local;
> float local_box_end = (rank + 1) * box_local;
> ```
> 
> **Critical**: Adjust density and laser positions to local coordinates:
> - Density step at global 54.0 → check which rank contains it, convert to local coords
> - Laser at global 17.0 → only add to rank that contains it, in local coords
> - Use **UNIFORM** density if simpler (all ranks have plasma)
> 
> Call `sim_new()` with local domain and MPI parameters:
> ```c
> sim_new( sim, nx_local, box_local, dt, tmax, ndump, species, n_species, rank, size );
> ```
> 
> ### 4. **main.c** - MPI initialization
> 
> - Add `#include <mpi.h>`
> - Call `MPI_Init()` at start
> - Get `rank` and `size`
> - Pass to `sim_init(&sim, rank, size)`
> - Only rank 0 prints status messages
> - Call `MPI_Finalize()` at end
> - Don't exit on energy error (print WARNING instead) so timing is shown
> 
> ### 5. **Makefile** - Use mpicc compiler
> 
> Change:
> ```makefile
> CC = mpicc
> TARGET = zpic_mpi
> ```
> 
> ## Expected Results:
> 
> ✅ **Speedup**: 6-8x faster than serial version (~1.5-2s vs ~10s)  
> ✅ **Compiles**: No errors with `make clean && make`  
> ✅ **Runs**: Completes without segfault  
> ⚠️ **Physics**: Energy conservation broken (expected - no communication)  
> ⚠️ **Particles**: Will disappear at domain boundaries (expected)  
> 
> ## Testing:
> 
> ```bash
> sbatch zpic_mpi.sh  # 4 nodes, 8 MPI ranks total
> ```
> 
> **Success Criteria**: Program runs to completion with significant speedup, even if energy conservation fails.
> 
> 


</details>

author: akash-nath29
body:
This pull request adds support for multi-turn conversations by implementing conversation history in both the backend (`backend/main.py`) and the frontend agent (`src/agent.js`). The agent now tracks and manages conversation history, includes it in requests to the backend for better context, and provides interactive commands for users to manage their session. The backend validates and utilizes this history to improve AI responses.

**Conversation History Support**

* Introduced a `ConversationMessage` model in the backend and extended the `ChatRequest` to accept an optional `conversation_history` array, allowing up to 20 previous messages for context.
* Backend chat endpoint now builds the message list by including system instructions, conversation history (if provided), and the current user prompt, enhancing multi-turn conversation support.
* The frontend agent tracks conversation history, trims it to a configurable maximum length, and formats it for backend requests. Assistant responses are summarized before being added to history for efficiency. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-89117af8b81bfeaf722beddae7606e64d109539455e3ee58d81f73e90bd228e6R46-R80) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-89117af8b81bfeaf722beddae7606e64d109539455e3ee58d81f73e90bd228e6R555-R577)
* When sending a chat request, the agent now includes the formatted conversation history if available, enabling the backend to generate more context-aware responses.

**Interactive Mode Enhancements**

* Added interactive commands: `clear`/`reset` to clear history, `history` to display conversation context, `refresh` to rescan the codebase, and `help` to show available commands, improving usability for multi-turn sessions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-89117af8b81bfeaf722beddae7606e64d109539455e3ee58d81f73e90bd228e6L541-R610) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-89117af8b81bfeaf722beddae7606e64d109539455e3ee58d81f73e90bd228e6L555-R669)

### Motivation
- Increase readability by making highlight and sentence text significantly larger and giving users simple size toggles.  
- Drive sentence generation with an AI backend so sentences use multiple random vocabulary items and chosen grammar patterns.  
- Provide a reading/audio toggle so sentences can be practiced by listening with text revealed on demand.  
- Standardize grammar options by hard-coding the initial set of grammar forms instead of relying on free-form user input.

### Description
- Hard-coded the initial grammar list into `GRAMMAR_FORMS` and switched sentence generation to pick a grammar and generate a sentence via the ChatGPT API in `_generate_sentence_with_chatgpt` (fallback logic included).

- Implemented Reading/Audio mode for the Sentence Generator with reveal and play controls (`_reveal_sentence_text`, `_play_audio_sentence`, `_open_audio_file`) and stored generated sentences in `generated_sentences`.  
- Updated the tone quiz to generate quiz sentences through ChatGPT via `_generate_quiz_sentence`, increased the quiz label font size, and removed user-entered grammar input in favor of the fixed list.

body:
### Motivation
- Reduce repeated `[NPC AI] decide` logs that were emitted every AI tick even when nothing meaningful changed.
- Preserve detailed AI tracing behind a dedicated verbose flag instead of the general `DEBUG_AI` toggle.
- Apply the deduplication defensively across all server NPC AI implementations to keep behavior consistent.

### Description
- Introduced a new environment flag `DEBUG_AI_VERBOSE` and used it for verbose AI logging instead of `DEBUG_AI` across `Server/state/config/systems/npcAiSystem.js`, `Server/state/systems/npcAiSystem.js`, and `Server/systems/npcAiSystem.js`.
- Added `meta.lastDecisionSnapshot` initialization in `ensureMetaDefaults` to track the last emitted decision snapshot per NPC.
- In `decideAction` the code now computes `decisionSnapshot = JSON.stringify({ state, currentCell, distanceToPlayer, healthPercent })` and logs `[NPC AI] decide` only when the snapshot differs from `meta.lastDecisionSnapshot`, then updates the meta field.
- Left the ability to enable verbose tracing via `DEBUG_AI_VERBOSE`, and preserved other debug behaviors (e.g. attack logging) unchanged except for using the new verbose flag where appropriate.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change.

author: albertdefusco
body:
One case where `model_dump()` does not list all potential keys that could be found in the config.toml is when a RootModel is used, for example in nested tables where any arbitrary number of tables of a certain type may be present.

```toml
[plugin.mapper.map.foo]
key = "foo"

[plugin.mapper.map.bar]
key = "bar"
```

Here the `map` table name is a RootModel to maintain a dictionary of Items where the key is inferred from the table name in the config.toml.

```python
class Item(BaseModel):
    key: Optional[str] = None

Mapping = RootModel[Dict[str, Item]]

class MappingPlugin(AnacondaBaseSettings, plugin_name="mapper"):
    map: Mapping = Mapping({})
``` 

In this scenario when an entry is dropped from `map` 

```python
plugin = MappingPlugin()
del plugin.map.root["foo"]
```

The dump of `plugin` can never be assumed to have exactly the same keys as when the configuration was read from disk. This would be equivalent to calling `delattr()` on a subclass of BaseModel after initialization.

author: copilot
body:
Adds push notification support for Android and iOS when pills are dispensed from a MedBox device.

## Implementation

**Data Model**
- `UserDeviceToken` entity stores FCM tokens per user with device type tracking
- Supports multiple devices per user with automatic token updates

**Notification Service**
- `PushNotificationService` sends FCM notifications on dispense events
- Auto-cleanup of invalid/expired tokens
- Graceful degradation when Firebase unconfigured

**REST API**
```java
POST /api/v1/notifications/register-token
{
  "fcmToken": "...",
  "deviceType": "ANDROID" | "IOS"
}

DELETE /api/v1/notifications/unregister-token?fcmToken={token}
```

**Integration Point**
- `DeviceWebSocketService.requestDispense()` triggers notifications after WebSocket dispatch
- Looks up user from device stack → sends to all registered tokens
- Non-blocking: notification failures don't affect dispense operations

**Notification Payload**
```
Title: "Pill Dispensed"
Body: "2 pill(s) dispensed from Kitchen Box, compartment 3"
Data: { boxName, compartmentNumber, pillsDispensed }
```

## Configuration

Requires `FIREBASE_CREDENTIALS_PATH` environment variable pointing to service account JSON. Optional - system continues without Firebase configured.

## Security

- Token ownership validated on unregistration
- All endpoints require OAuth2 authentication
- Credentials excluded from version control via `.gitignore`

body:
## Summary

Implements Redis Streams as a streaming DataFrame source as described in issue #120.

## Changes

### New Functions

- **`read_stream()`** - Read entries from a single stream into DataFrame
  - Uses XRANGE for non-blocking reads
  - Uses XREAD for blocking reads
  - Uses XREADGROUP for consumer group reads

- **`scan_stream()`** - Lazy version returning LazyFrame

- **`iter_stream()`** - Sync iterator yielding DataFrame batches

- **`stream_batches()`** - Async iterator yielding DataFrame batches

- **`ack_entries()`** - Manually acknowledge messages in consumer groups

### Features

- Consumer group support with automatic group creation
- Blocking reads for real-time tailing (`block_ms` parameter)
- Manual or automatic message acknowledgment (`auto_ack`)
- Entry ID parsing into timestamp and sequence columns
- Schema casting for typed columns
- Custom column naming

### Tests

- 16 comprehensive tests in `tests/test_streams.py`
- Tests for basic reads, count limits, ID ranges
- Tests for consumer groups, manual ack, multiple consumers
- Tests for batch iteration (sync and async)

### Documentation

- Full guide at `docs/guide/streams.md`
- API reference with examples
- Added to mkdocs navigation

## Example Usage

```python
import polars_redis as redis

# Basic read
df = redis.read_stream(
    "redis://localhost",
    stream="events",
    schema={"user_id": pl.Utf8, "action": pl.Utf8},
)

# Consumer group with auto-ack
df = redis.read_stream(
    "redis://localhost",
    stream="events",
    group="analytics",
    consumer="worker-1",
    auto_ack=True,
)

# Continuous batch iteration
for batch_df in redis.iter_stream(
    "redis://localhost",
    stream="events",
    batch_size=100,
    block_ms=1000,
):
    process(batch_df)
```

## Differences from Existing `scan_streams`/`read_streams`

The existing functions scan **multiple streams** by key pattern. This PR adds functions for:

1. **Single stream consumption** with consumer groups
2. **Blocking reads** for real-time tailing
3. **Continuous streaming** with batch iterators

Closes #120

author: brunoerg
body:
### Problem 

When a node is shut down while network activity is disabled (e.g. via -networkactive=0 or `setnetworkactive` false), `anchors.dat` is overwritten with an empty list. This happens because `StopNodes()` collects anchors via `GetCurrentBlockRelayOnlyConns()`, which returns nothing when there are no active connections. The node then loses its anchors and cannot reconnect to them on the next startup.

### Fix 

- In `SetNetworkActive(false)`, save the current block-relay-only connections into `m_anchors` before the connections are closed, so the anchor list is preserved even after the network is deactivated.
- In `StopNodes()`, if the network is inactive and m_anchors is non-empty, use those stored anchors as the source for anchors.dat instead of the (empty) live connection list. Also skip `DumpAnchors` entirely when the network is inactive and there is nothing to write.

Also, log that "X anchors will be tried for connections" only if network is active.

*December 3, 2025*

Welcome to Django 6.0!

These release notes cover the :ref:`new features <whats-new-6.0>`, as well as
some :ref:`backwards incompatible changes <backwards-incompatible-6.0>` you
should be aware of when upgrading from Django 5.2 or earlier. We've

<deprecated-features-6.0>`.

See the :doc:`/howto/upgrade-version` guide if you're updating an existing
project.

Python compatibility
====================

Django 6.0 supports Python 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14. We **highly recommend**, and
only officially support, the latest release of each series.

The Django 5.2.x series is the last to support Python 3.10 and 3.11.

Third-party library support for older versions of Django
========================================================

Following the release of Django 6.0, we suggest that third-party app authors
drop support for all versions of Django prior to 5.2. At that time, you should
be able to run your package's tests using ``python -Wd`` so that deprecation
warnings appear. After making the deprecation warning fixes, your app should be
compatible with Django 6.0.

.. _whats-new-6.0:

What's new in Django 6.0
========================

Content Security Policy support
-------------------------------

Built-in support for the :ref:`Content Security Policy (CSP) <security-csp>`
standard is now available, making it easier to protect web applications against
content injection attacks such as cross-site scripting (XSS). CSP allows
declaring trusted sources of content by giving browsers strict rules about
which scripts, styles, images, or other resources can be loaded.

CSP policies can now be enforced or monitored directly using built-in tools:
headers are added via the
:class:`~django.middleware.csp.ContentSecurityPolicyMiddleware`, nonces are
supported through the :func:`~django.template.context_processors.csp` context
processor, and policies are configured using the :setting:`SECURE_CSP` and
:setting:`SECURE_CSP_REPORT_ONLY` settings.

These settings accept Python dictionaries and support Django-provided constants
for clarity and safety. For example::

    from django.utils.csp import CSP

    SECURE_CSP = {
        "default-src": [CSP.SELF],
        "script-src": [CSP.SELF, CSP.NONCE],
        "img-src": [CSP.SELF, "https:"],
    }

The resulting ``Content-Security-Policy`` header would be set to:

.. code-block:: text

    default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-SECRET'; img-src 'self' https:

To get started, follow the :doc:`CSP how-to guide </howto/csp>`. For in-depth
guidance, see the :ref:`CSP security overview <security-csp>` and the
:doc:`reference docs </ref/csp>`, which include details about decorators to
override or disable policies on a per-view basis.

Template Partials
-----------------

The :ref:`Django Template Language <template-language-intro>` now supports
:ref:`template partials <template-partials>`, making it easier to encapsulate
and reuse small named fragments within a template file. The new tags
:ttag:`{% partialdef %} <partialdef>` and :ttag:`{% partial %} <partial>`
define a partial and render it, respectively.

Partials can also be referenced using the ``template_namepartial_name`` syntax
with :func:`~django.template.Engine.get_template`,
:func:`~django.shortcuts.render`, :ttag:`{% include %}<include>`, and other
template-loading tools, enabling more modular and maintainable templates
without needing to split components into separate files.

A `migration guide`_ is available if you're updating from the
:pypi:`django-template-partials` third-party package.

.. _migration guide: https://github.com/carltongibson/django-template-partials/blob/main/Migration.md

Background Tasks
----------------

Django now includes a built-in Tasks framework for running code outside the
HTTP request–response cycle. This enables offloading work, such as sending
emails or processing data, to background workers.

The framework provides task definition, validation, queuing, and result
handling. Django guarantees consistent behavior for creating and managing
tasks, while the responsibility for running them continues to belong to
external worker processes.

Tasks are defined using the :func:`~django.tasks.task` decorator::

    from django.core.mail import send_mail
    from django.tasks import task


    task
    def email_users(emails, subject, message):
        return send_mail(subject, message, None, emails)

Once defined, tasks can be enqueued through a configured backend::

    email_users.enqueue(
        emails=["userexample.com"],
        subject="You have a message",
        message="Hello there!",
    )

Backends are configured via the :setting:`TASKS` setting. The :ref:`two
built-in backends <task-available-backends>` included in this release are
primarily intended for development and testing.

Django handles task creation and queuing, but does not provide a worker
mechanism to run tasks. Execution must be managed by external infrastructure,
such as a separate process or service.

</ref/tasks>` for API details.

author: whortleberrybearer
body:
## Description

This PR adds a Firebase Callable Function (`syncPubsOnDemand`) that enables authorized administrators to trigger pub data syncs remotely on-demand, complementing the existing scheduled sync functionality.

The implementation includes:
- New callable function with full authorization, parameter validation, and error handling
- Support for both full sync and update sync modes with existing parameters
- Environment variable configuration for admin user authorization
- Updated GitHub Actions workflows to include the new environment variable
- Comprehensive documentation in READMEs

## Motivation and Context

The pub sync system previously ran only on a scheduled basis. Manual syncs required running a local script with a development environment setup. This created operational friction when:
- Data quality issues need immediate correction
- Emergency updates are required
- Testing/verifying sync logic changes
- Recovering from failed scheduled syncs

This change enables administrators to trigger syncs remotely via Firebase CLI or SDK without requiring local environment access.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- ✅ TypeScript compilation successful (no errors)
- ✅ Function builds correctly to JavaScript
- ✅ OpenSpec validation passed with `--strict` flag
- ✅ All environment variables renamed consistently across codebase
- ✅ GitHub Actions workflows updated and validated

**Manual testing pending deployment:**
- Deploy function with `WETHERSPOONING_ADMIN_USER_ID` configured
- Test via Firebase CLI with authorized and unauthorized users
- Verify parameter validation for both sync modes
- Confirm error handling and logging

## Screenshots (if appropriate):

N/A - Backend function implementation

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)

- [x] My change requires a change to the documentation.
- [x] I have updated the documentation accordingly.

## Related Issue

Related to scheduled-data-sync capability. Addresses operational need for on-demand pub sync execution.

### **User description** ## Summary Adds full support for UniFi's v2 Firewall Policies API (Traffic & Firewall Rules), which is the modern replacement for legacy firewall rules. **Related Issue:** #11 ## New Features ### Pydantic Models (`src/models/firewall_policy.py`) - `FirewallPolicy` - Complete model for v2 firewall policies - Supports all policy attributes: zones, matching targets, protocols, actions ### MCP Tools (`src/tools/firewall_policies.py`) | Tool | Description | |------|-------------| | `list_firewall_policies` | List all Traffic & Firewall Rules for a site | | `get_firewall_policy` | Get details for a specific policy | | `create_firewall_policy` | Create a new policy (requires `confirm=True`) | | `update_firewall_policy` | Update an existing policy (requires `confirm=True`) | | `delete_firewall_policy` | Delete a policy (requires `confirm=True`) | ### Safety Features - All mutating operations require explicit `confirm=True` - `dry_run=True` mode for previewing changes - Works with local gateway API (`UNIFI_API_TYPE=local`) ## API Endpoints Used ``` GET /v2/api/site/{site}/trafficroutes # List policies GET /v2/api/site/{site}/trafficroutes/{id} # Get policy POST /v2/api/site/{site}/trafficroutes # Create policy PUT /v2/api/site/{site}/trafficroutes/{id} # Update policy DELETE /v2/api/site/{site}/trafficroutes/{id} # Delete policy ``` ## Example Usage ```python # List all firewall policies policies = await mcp.call_tool("list_firewall_policies", {"site_id": "default"}) # Create a policy to block IoT from LAN await mcp.call_tool("create_firewall_policy", { "site_id": "default", "name": "Block IoT to LAN", "action": "BLOCK", "source_zone_id": "iot-zone-id", "destination_zone_id": "lan-zone-id", "confirm": True }) ``` ## Checklist - author: paulgessinger
body:
This pull request introduces comprehensive support for managing trashed documents across the app. It adds new API endpoints and repository methods for fetching, restoring, and permanently deleting trashed documents, updates the UI to include a dedicated Trash view in Settings, and provides appropriate localization. The changes ensure that users can view, restore, or permanently delete documents from the trash, with full support in both the backend and frontend.

**Trashed Document Management**

* Added new methods to the `Repository` protocol and its implementations (`ApiRepository`, `TransientRepository`, `NullRepository`, and `PreviewRepository`) for fetching trashed documents, restoring them, and emptying the trash. The `TransientRepository` now moves deleted documents to a `trashedDocuments` collection and supports restoring or permanently deleting them.

* Introduced new endpoints in `Endpoint.swift` for trash-related actions, including listing trashed documents and performing restore or empty actions. Added corresponding unit tests to verify endpoint construction.
**User Interface Enhancements**

* Added a new `TrashView` in the Settings section, allowing users to view trashed documents, restore them, or permanently delete them (individually or in bulk). The view handles loading, error reporting, and supports edit mode for multi-selection. 

**Localization**

* Added new localized strings for the Trash UI, including titles, button labels, and confirmation dialogs.

**Changelog**

* Updated the changelog to note the addition of trashed document management.

Closes #118

body: **Purpose of this pull request:** This PR fixes following bugs/feat requests: - The grid elements should probably be clickable/link somewhere like they do on github. Also, does this grid stay in sync? If it doesn't, then we should probably note the date that the grid data was last updated in both the UI and CLI (let's do that first). - - The repocard status doesn't seem to display, only the emoji. Also I probably don't want the emoji or status to be set at all. Also, I don't think they should be set in the site config, they should just be part of the props for the component. - - We should probably just move it to the main developer (not hide it behind hovering) or under the card or something. - - The grid view hover is delayed and at first I didn't notice that anything got displayed at all. - - The contribution-activity badge on-hover seems pointless, we can remove it. - - Since I can't actually click the profile card I can't verify this rn, but please make sure the links all work there. Including, ideally, to the [@organization](https://github.com/organization) links (eg mine are [@accretional](https://github.com/accretional) and [@google](https://github.com/google) and [@microsoft](https://github.com/microsoft)). - - I can't actually click or select anything on the profile card because it converts to the contribution grid view when I hover over it. Probably we should move the grid elsewhere in the UI and get rid of this hover effect. - - We properly import location and organization but don't import the user's links (checkout mine on my profile, I have three, [accretional.com](http://accretional.com/), [in/fred-weitendorf-40b505b6](https://www.linkedin.com/in/fred-weitendorf-40b505b6/), https://statue.dev/) - it would be good to also import these. **(optional) Issues fixed**: fixes #114 ## IMPORTANT - UI CHANGE DEMONSTRATION If making a change that changes the existing UI, or adds/changes new UI elements like components, themes, or templates, you MUST include screenshots or demos/recordings of your changes: Screenshots: Site preview link: ## Other things worth discussing regarding PR: Anything not covered by previous sections

alloc_utils has platform-dependent and platform-independent logic. We've talked about rewriting some or all of the existing logic that simply just shells out to ip(8) to use netlink instead. We could just rewrite the existing logic directly, but we are also wanting to expose cvdalloc to more people soon, so we don't want to make too many changes too quickly so we get a cleaner signal if a cvdalloc rollout goes awry.

Instead, we pull out the collection of platform-dependent logic into a platform "driver"; the existing logic becomes the iproute2 driver and a future driver will use netlink directly. This will become relevant too in the (distant?) future where we want to make the cuttlefish host tools more portable.

body: Stacked PRs: * #3606 * __->__#3585 * #3584 * #3583 * #3582 * #3581 * #3580 * #3579 --- --- --- ### [mxfp8 moe training] add benchmark for e2e mxfp8 EP pipeline This stack creates a set of differentiable MXFP8 expert parallel primitives for MoE training: - a2a_dispatch - permute - unpermute - a2a_combine The key idea is instead of waiting to quantize to MXFP8 until directly before the grouped GEMMs, we can quantize earlier, before the a2a collectives, to speed up these exposed comms. This requires staying in MXFP8 through the token permutation, then feeding those permuted fp8 data + scales into the MXFP8 grouped GEMM, which produces bf16 outputs. We do this in both the forward pass and backward pass. ### Design Each color corresponds to a separate autograd function: ### Benchmarks This benchmark measures the **entire forward + backward pass of the full EP pipeline**: Forward: - a2a_dispatch - permute - MXFP8 grouped GEMM - unpermute - a2a_combine Backward: - a2a_combine backward() - unpermute backward() - MXFP8 grouped GEMM backward() - permute backward() - a2a_dispatch backward() For DeepSeekV3 shapes we see: - 1.4x speedup over vanilla bf16 pipeline (with torch._grouped_mm) - 1.22x speedup over existing torchao pipeline (with bf16 all2alls, mxfp8 grouped GEMMs) Note this is WITHOUT the mxfp8 grouped GEMM improvements landing in pytorch core soon, so we expect even higher speedups then! We have lower speedups than usual right now due to improvments landing to bf16 grouped gemm but none to mxfp8 grouped gemm yet. #### Versus vanilla bf16 pipeline: ``` Expert Parallelism Pipeline This PR fixes a bug where the query plan parser failed to correctly visualize certain MySQL explain plans. The issue was caused by the regex `estimationPattern` in `src/services/plan-service.ts` strictly expecting decimal values for costs and integer values for rows.

MySQL explain plans can contain:
- Integer costs (e.g., `cost=368517`).
- Scientific notation for rows (e.g., `rows=1.48e+6`).
- Float rows (e.g., `rows=4.16`).

The fix introduces a more flexible `numberPattern` that handles all these formats.

**Changes:**
- `src/services/plan-service.ts`: Updated `estimationPattern` to support scientific notation and integers for cost and rows attributes.

author: dani1996dani
body:
This PR introduces the core functionality for the proposal ingestion and AI extraction technical assessment. 
It establishes a robust, asynchronous architecture designed to handle bulk file uploads reliably on a serverless platform (Vercel).

# Key Architectural Decisions:
- Client-Side Orchestration: To avoid serverless timeouts and provide granular UI feedback, the frontend orchestrates the processing queue. It uploads all files in a single batch (uploadProposals) and then triggers the AI extraction (processProposal) for each file individually, with a concurrency limit of 3 to manage API rate limits.
- Gemini 2.5 Flash (Native PDF): Leveraged Gemini's native multimodal capabilities to process PDFs directly, eliminating the need for client-side rendering or server-side image processing dependencies (canvas, gm), which simplifies the stack and deployment.
- Database as Source of Truth: The system is resumable. If the user refreshes the page, the client queue will automatically pick up any PENDING proposals from the database and continue processing.
- Deduplication via SHA-256: A hash of the file content is stored to prevent re-processing of duplicate files, saving cost and time.
- Glass-Box AI: Implemented a "Confidence + Reasoning" schema to provide full transparency into the AI's decision-making process, addressing the "transparency matters more" requirement.

# Features Implemented:
- File Handling:
  - Bulk file upload with size validation (10MB).
  - File storage via Supabase Storage.
- Backend:
  - uploadProposals action for fast, parallelized ingestion.
  - processProposal action for idempotent, single-file AI extraction.
  - retryProposal action for graceful error handling.
- Frontend:
  - UploadZone for drag-and-drop.
  - DashboardTable with real-time optimistic updates, skeleton loaders for PENDING items, and a live stats header.
  - useProposalQueue custom hook to manage the client-side processing logic.
- UI/UX:
  - Added Sonner for toast notifications.
  - Implemented a ConfidenceBadge component for visual feedback.
  - Added a manual "Retry" button for failed jobs.

author: vacinc
body:
## Problem

Discord voice messages have empty `content` field — the audio is in the attachment. The code used nullish coalescing (`??`) to fall back to the media placeholder, but empty string (`""`) is not nullish, so voice messages were being silently dropped.

## Solution

Changed `??` to `||` so empty string falls through to `media?.placeholder`, which correctly returns `<media:audio>` for audio attachments.

## Testing

- Sent Discord voice messages before fix: dropped with 'empty content'
- After fix: voice messages are received, transcribed (via `transcribeAudio` config), and processed correctly

## Related

This fix enables the `routing.transcribeAudio` config to work with Discord voice messages.

## Vercel Speed Insights Integration

Successfully implemented Vercel Speed Insights for the RankMe project (Vite + React + TypeScript application).

### What Was Implemented

Integrated Vercel Speed Insights to track and monitor Core Web Vitals and performance metrics for the application deployed on Vercel.

### Files Modified

1. **package.json** - Added `@vercel/speed-insights` dependency (v1.3.1)
2. **src/App.tsx** - Integrated SpeedInsights component

### Changes Made

#### 1. Added Package Dependency
- Installed `@vercel/speed-insights` package using npm
- This package is automatically updated when the app is deployed to Vercel

#### 2. Integrated SpeedInsights Component in App.tsx
- Imported `SpeedInsights` from `@vercel/speed-insights/react`
- Added the `<SpeedInsights />` component inside the App component's JSX structure
- Placed it after the BrowserRouter and inside the TooltipProvider to ensure it runs on the client-side after all providers are initialized
- This placement ensures proper tracking of all routes and performance metrics throughout the application

### Why These Implementation Choices

1. **React Implementation**: Used the `/react` export from the package instead of framework-specific implementations (like `/next` for Next.js) because this project uses a vanilla React setup with React Router and Vite, not Next.js.

2. **Component Placement**: Added the component after the BrowserRouter to ensure all routes are properly tracked. It's placed inside the TooltipProvider to maintain the provider hierarchy and ensure client-side execution.

3. **No Manual Route Tracking Needed**: Unlike older versions of the package, the React SpeedInsights component automatically tracks route changes when used with client-side routing, so explicit route props are not needed in this case.

### How It Works

Once deployed to Vercel:
1. The Speed Insights component automatically injects a tracking script on the page
2. The script collects Core Web Vitals metrics (LCP, FID, CLS, etc.)
3. Data is sent to Vercel's Speed Insights dashboard
4. Performance metrics can be viewed in the Vercel dashboard under the Speed Insights tab

### Prerequisites for Full Setup

To complete the setup in the Vercel dashboard:
1. Enable Speed Insights in the Vercel project dashboard (Speed Insights tab → Enable)
2. Deploy the application to Vercel
3. After deployment, the `/_vercel/speed-insights/script.js` endpoint will be available
4. Once users visit the site, metrics will start appearing in the dashboard after a few days

Jira: CCFRI-6944

Using fixed URLS in many cases as router **pushes** to go "backward" breaks the built-in mechanic of `$router.push()` which results in "backward loops" between two pages.

This PR addresses these problems.

Update: While it would have been nice to have an intuitive backwards navigation feature, the fix required touching every single instance where we "push backwards" instead of "go backwards." The resulting testing effort would have been literally anywhere we go "back" from. So, I chose the path of least resistance.

## Summary
## Summary

When connecting a ZMK-compatible keyboard that hasn't been connected for a while (or is connecting for the first time), creating a new layer and attempting to switch to it does not work. The keyboard view refreshes but remains on the first layer instead of switching to the newly created layer.

## Environment

- **Browser:** Chrome
- **Keyboard:** ZMK-compatible keyboard
- **Platform:** ZMK Studio

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ensure the keyboard has not been connected to ZMK Studio recently (or is connecting for the first time)
2. Connect the keyboard to ZMK Studio
3. Create a new layer using the "Add Layer" functionality
4. Click on the newly created layer to switch to it

## Expected Behavior

After creating a new layer, clicking on it should immediately switch the keyboard view to display that layer's keymap.

## Actual Behavior

After creating a new layer and clicking on it:
- The keyboard view appears to refresh
- The view remains on the first layer (Layer 0)
- The newly created layer is not selected/displayed

## Workaround

Refresh the browser page, then reconnect to the keyboard. After doing this, layer switching works correctly for all layers including the newly created one.

## Additional Context

- No errors appear in the browser console when this issue occurs
- This only affects newly created layers during the initial connection session
- Existing layers and subsequent connections work correctly after a page refresh
- The issue seems to be related to state synchronization on first connection

author: simiondolha
body:
## Summary

Fixes #24856 - Self-hosted setup: /v2/event-types returns 500 – license check fails with HTML response

The `DeploymentsService.checkLicense()` method was crashing with `"Unexpected token '<'"` when the license server returned HTML instead of JSON. This caused 500 Internal Server Error on `/v2/event-types` and other API v2 endpoints for self-hosted deployments.

## Root Cause

The original code called `response.json()` directly without:
1. Checking if the response was successful (`response.ok`)
2. Validating the `Content-Type` header
3. Wrapping in try-catch for error handling

When the license server returned an error page (HTML), `JSON.parse` threw a `SyntaxError` which propagated as a 500 error.

## Changes

### `apps/api/v2/src/modules/deployments/deployments.service.ts`

- **Add 10-second timeout** using `AbortSignal.timeout()` to prevent hanging requests
- **Check `response.ok`** before attempting to parse JSON
- **Validate `Content-Type`** header contains `application/json`
- **Validate JSON structure** - `status` field must be a boolean
- **Wrap in try-catch** - return `false` on any error (fail-closed)
- **Only cache successful validations** - don't cache failures so retries work immediately after fixing config
- **Add logging** via NestJS Logger for debugging

### `apps/api/v2/src/modules/auth/strategies/api-auth/api-auth.strategy.ts`

- **Improve error message** with debugging hints for self-hosted admins:
  ```
  "License validation failed. Check CALCOM_LICENSE_KEY and GET_LICENSE_KEY_URL configuration."
  ```

### `apps/api/v2/src/modules/deployments/deployments.service.spec.ts` (new)

- **18 comprehensive unit tests** covering:
  - E2E mode bypass
  - Missing license key
  - Cached results / corrupted cache
  - HTTP error responses (4xx, 5xx)
  - HTML responses (text/html, missing Content-Type)
  - Invalid JSON structure (missing status, non-boolean status)
  - Valid/invalid license responses
  - Network errors and timeouts
  - Caching behavior (cache hits, no cache on failures)

## Before vs After

| Scenario | Before | After |
|----------|--------|-------|
| License server returns HTML | 500 Internal Server Error | 401 Unauthorized (with helpful message) |
| License server unreachable | Hangs indefinitely | Timeout after 10s, returns 401 |
| License server returns 404 | 500 (JSON parse error) | 401 Unauthorized |
| Invalid license | May crash depending on response | 401 Unauthorized |
| Valid license | Works | Works (no change) |

## Test Plan

- [x] Unit tests pass (18 test cases)
- [ ] Manual test on self-hosted Docker deployment with:
  - Valid license key
  - Invalid license key
  - Unreachable license server (wrong `GET_LICENSE_KEY_URL`)
  - License server returning HTML error page

## Configuration Reference

For self-hosted deployments, ensure these environment variables are set:

```env
CALCOM_LICENSE_KEY=your-license-key
GET_LICENSE_KEY_URL=https://console.cal.com/api/license
```

author: copilot
body:
Implements a CMake module to enable compiler caching via ccache or sccache, reducing recompilation time.

## Changes

- **`tools/cmake/meta_cache.cmake`**: New module with auto-detection and explicit backend selection
  - `ENABLE`: Boolean flag to enable/disable caching
  - `BACKEND`: Select `auto` (default, prefers ccache), `ccache`, or `sccache`
  - Sets `CMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER` and `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER`
  - Warns if requested tool not found, continues without caching

- **`README.md`**: Updated section 2.7.1 to reflect compiler cache support for both tools

## Usage

```cmake
include(meta_cache)
meta_cache(ENABLE ON)                    # Auto-detect
meta_cache(ENABLE ON BACKEND ccache)     # Explicit ccache
meta_cache(ENABLE ON BACKEND sccache)    # Explicit sccache
```

Follows existing module patterns (meta_sanitizers, meta_coverage) for consistency.

Implement comprehensive auto-stop functionality for seamless updates across macOS, Windows, and Linux installers.

Changes by platform:

**macOS:**
- New: pre-install-stop.sh - Stops Shop Manager + embedded PostgreSQL
- Enhanced: shop-manager launcher with port conflict detection
- Better error messages showing actual failure reasons
- Graceful shutdown with 5s timeout → force kill fallback

**Windows (Inno Setup):**
- Enhanced: PrepareToInstall() now stops PostgreSQL processes
- Cleans up PID files in %USERPROFILE%\.shopmanager
- New: stop-shop-manager.bat manual helper script
- Added detailed logging

**Linux (DEB/RPM):**
- Enhanced: preinst.sh and rpm-preinst.sh for embedded PostgreSQL
- Stops both systemd service AND standalone JAR execution
- Handles multiple user home directories (for root installs)
- New: stop-shop-manager.sh manual helper script

**Common improvements:**
- Stop both Java process AND embedded PostgreSQL (port 5433)
- Clean up PID files and PostgreSQL lock files
- Verify ports 8081 and 5433 are freed before proceeding
- Graceful shutdown with fallback to force kill
- Clear status messages and error reporting

**Result:**
Seamless updates on all platforms - old version auto-stops during installation, preventing port conflicts and file locks.

Fixes: macOS "failed to start" error showing old instance's log

body:
### Motivation
- Choose an appropriate "active" tuned metric per model after tuning all metrics so live projections use the best-fitting metric without refactoring the pipeline.
- Preserve all per-metric tuning results while promoting a single metric into the active params for each model.
- Surface provenance for which tuned params were used in downstream outputs to aid debugging and reporting.
- Keep existing model/tuning math and pipeline behavior unchanged except for selecting and reporting the active metric.

### Description
- Add `src/pipelines/tuning_policy.py` with `default_active_metric_for_model` to encode per-model metric policy and wire it into the CLI tuning flow so `tune --model all --metric all --apply-best` promotes the policy-chosen metric.
- Extend tuning to print `Applied ACTIVE metric=<metric> for model=<model_id>` when promoting tuned params and continue saving all per-metric tuned params in the DB (no change to tuning math).
- Introduce `ModelParamsResolution` and `resolve_model_params_with_metadata` in `src/pipelines/model_params.py` to return `params`, `params_source`, and `tuned_metric_used`, and propagate that metadata into `run_rankings`, `schedule`, and `matchups` outputs and metadata.
- Add `params_source` and `tuned_metric_used` fields to exports and contracts, update schedule workbook metadata to include these fields, and add CLI printing of provenance for matchup predictions.

### Testing
- Ran `pytest tests/pipelines/test_tuned_params.py tests/pipelines/test_schedule.py tests/pipelines/test_run_rankings.py` and all tests passed (16 passed).
- Existing unit tests that exercise tuning persistence, schedule projection, rankings, and schedule Excel/report behavior were updated and validated to ensure metadata fields are present and the active-metric policy is applied.
- Verified that promotion logging (`Applied ACTIVE metric=...`) prints when `--apply-best` is used and that schedule/matchup outputs report `params_source` and `tuned_metric_used` correctly.
- Ensured no model math or tuning math was modified during these changes and pipeline behavior remains compatible with existing callers.

author: copilot
body:
Configuration was scattered across multiple files with silent fallbacks masking errors. Consolidated hardware settings, button mappings, and system configurations into a single `config.json` with explicit validation.

## Changes

**Configuration consolidation:**
- Merged `buttons.json`, `systems.json`, and hardcoded constants into unified `config.json`
- Structure: `hardware` (LEDs, brightness, FPS) → `paths` (FIFO, state file) → `buttons` (mappings, patterns) → `defaults` (menu color, attract mode) → `systems` (per-system colors, layouts)

**Removed silent fallbacks:**
- `default_menu_color()`: raises `ValueError` if not configured (was: return hardcoded blue)
- `default_attract_mode()`: raises `ValueError` if not configured (was: return "breath")
- `anim_game_start()`: raises `ValueError` if system has no accent (was: fallback green)
- `idle_attract_generator()`: raises `ValueError` if no patterns configured (was: fallback rainbow/breath)

**Color parsing abstraction:**
```python
# Now supports three formats consistently
parse_color_dict({"r": 255, "g": 0, "b": 0, "br": 36})    # Dict
parse_color_string("#ff0000:100")                          # Hex string
parse_color_tuple([0, 0, 255, 40])                         # Tuple
```

**Code organization:**
- Separated concerns: `FRAME GENERATORS` (idle loops) → `ATTRACT PATTERN GENERATORS` (pattern functions) → `EVENT ANIMATIONS` (one-shots) → `ANIMATION HELPERS` (shared utilities)
- Renamed helper functions with underscore prefix: `_wipe_frames()`, `_fade_all()`
- Unified configuration loading into single `load_config()` function

**Documentation:**
- Updated `BUTTONS_README.md` to document unified configuration structure and all supported color formats

author: bdraco
body:
# What does this implement/fix?

Eliminate heap allocation when publishing the DSMR telegram to a text sensor.

**Before:** `publish_state(std::string(this->telegram_, this->bytes_read_))` creates a temporary `std::string`, causing a heap allocation for every telegram received.

**After:** `publish_state(this->telegram_, this->bytes_read_)` calls the new `const char*` overload directly, avoiding the temporary.

While DSMR telegrams can be large, Home Assistant limits text sensor state to 255 bytes. This eliminates a 255-byte heap allocation every few seconds, which reduces heap fragmentation on long-running ESP8266 devices.

author: copilot
body:
Strawberry crashes when playing Spotify tracks because Spotify was incorrectly included in `Song::stream_url_can_expire()`. The code path in `Player::UnPause()` checks both `url_handlers_->CanHandle()` and `song.stream_url_can_expire()` (which incorrectly returned `true` for Spotify), causing failures when no handler is registered.

## Root Cause

Unlike Tidal and Qobuz which fetch temporary stream URLs from APIs, Spotify URIs are permanent identifiers (`spotify:track:...`) that:
- Don't expire and don't need refreshing
- Are handled directly by gst-plugin-spotify
- Only require access token refresh via `EngineBase::UpdateSpotifyAccessToken()`

## Solution

Remove `Source::Spotify` from the `stream_url_can_expire()` method in `src/core/song.cpp`. This single-line change prevents the URL handler logic from executing for Spotify tracks, eliminating the crash.

## Changes Made

```cpp
// Before: Spotify incorrectly marked as having expiring URLs
bool Song::stream_url_can_expire() const { 
  return d->source_ == Source::Tidal || d->source_ == Source::Qobuz || d->source_ == Source::Spotify; 
}

// After: Only Tidal and Qobuz have expiring stream URLs
bool Song::stream_url_can_expire() const { 
  return d->source_ == Source::Tidal || d->source_ == Source::Qobuz; 
}
```

This ensures Spotify tracks bypass the URL refresh logic entirely, allowing gst-plugin-spotify to handle playback directly without requiring a URL handler infrastructure.

body:
# Describe the PR

Fixes SSR errors that occur when building the VitePress documentation site. Errors included "document is not defined", "cannot destructure property hide of undefined", and "Object.groupBy is not a function".

**Browser API Guards**

author: nigelnelson
body:
The torchvision/pyav path in get_frames_by_timestamps now reads frames until the final requested timestamp and then selects the closest loaded frame for each requested timestamp. This prevents early exit when the number of loaded frames equals the number of requested timestamps and avoids returning the first contiguous frames after seek instead of the requested ones. It also raises a clear error if no frames were loaded.

This fix is helpful for intentional downsampling. If a user has 10Hz video and wants to sample 5 frames at 5Hz, the current torchvision/pyav backend returns the wrong frames.

## Example (10Hz video)
At 10Hz, each frame is 0.1s apart: frame 0 = 0.0s, frame 1 = 0.1s, frame 2 = 0.2s, etc.
Requested frames: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 (timestamps 0.0s, 0.2s, 0.4s, 0.6s, 0.8s)

Before: the loop stops after loading 5 frames and returns the first 5 loaded frames.
Returned frames: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4
Returned timestamps: 0.0s, 0.1s, 0.2s, 0.3s, 0.4s

After: the loop reads until 0.8s and maps each requested timestamp to the closest loaded frame.
Returned frames: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8
Returned timestamps: 0.0s, 0.2s, 0.4s, 0.6s, 0.8s
